articleTitle: Modeling the interfacial profiles in III-V VLS axial nanowire heterostructures based on group V interchange
abstract: abstract-Interfacial abruptness in axial heterostructures within III-V nanowires (NWs) grown by the vapor-liquid-solid (VLS) method is affected by the reservoir effect in catalyst droplets which broadens the heterointerfaces. Here, we present a model which provides explicitly the interfacial profiles in double NW heterostructures based on group V interchange of any composition, and fit the data on Au-catalyzed $\operatorname{InP} / \operatorname{In} s \mathrm{~s} / \mathrm{InP}$, self-catalyzed $\mathrm{GaAs}_{0.6} \mathrm{P}_{0.4} / \mathbf{G a}_{x} \mathrm{AsxP}_{1-\mathrm{x}} / \mathrm{GaAs}_{0.6} \mathrm{P}_{0.4}$ and $\mathrm{GaP} / \mathrm{GaAs}_{\mathrm{x}} \mathrm{P}_{1-\mathrm{x}} / \mathrm{GaP}$ axial NW heterostructures.

articleTitle: High power Q-switched and gain-switched fiber lasers
abstract: A compact all-fiber passively Q-switched and gain-switched (QSGS) Ytterbium-doped lasers are demonstrated. The basic laser architecture consists of two nested cavities encloses in fiber Bragg gratings (FBG) with different central wavelengths in the range of 1060 nm, this laser architecture has remarkable flexibility and makes it possible to create many variations of pulsed laser sources with unique generation parameters. Several types of pulsed lasers were demonstrated: single-mode ($\mathrm{M}^{2}\lt 1.2$), few-mode ($\mathrm{M}^{2}\lt 2$) and multimode ($\mathrm{M}^{2}\lt 7$) with average output powers of $130 \mathrm{~W}, 500 \mathrm{~W}$ and 1 kW and pulse energies of $1.5 \mathrm{~mJ}, 2.7 \mathrm{~mJ}$ and 7.2 mJ, respectively, with a pulse width in the range of $100 \mathrm{~ns}-300 \mathrm{~ns}$. To optimize the laser performance, a special numerical model has been developed that takes into account the basic laser parameters and adequately predict its experimental characteristics. The results of the work demonstrate the prospects of using a dual-cavity QSGS all-fiber pulsed laser architecture to create high performance pulsed laser sources.

articleTitle: Thermal Lensing and Laser-Induced Damage in Special Pure Chalcogenide Glasses under CW and Pulsed Mid-IR Irradiations
abstract: Special pure chalcogenide glass (ChG) is an attractive material for mid-infrared (mid-IR) optical fibers and fiber lasers. This report is devoted to studying thermo-optical lensing (TOL) and laser-induced damage (LID) in ternary and quaternary ChGs based on sulfides and selenides ($\mathbf{G e}, \mathbf{A s}, \mathbf{S b,}, \mathrm{Ga}$ and $\mathbf{I n}$) doped with $\mathbf{T b}^{\mathbf{3 +}}$ and $\mathrm{Pr}^{3+}$ ions. The thermal nonlinear refractive index of the ChG was determined by the Z-scan technique using a quasi-CW Tm-doped fiber laser at 1908 nm. The repetitively-pulsed $\mathrm{Ho}^{3+}:$ YAG laser at $2.1 \mu \mathrm{m}$ and a ZGP-based optical parametric oscillator at 3.8/4.65 $\mu \mathrm{m}$ were applied for LID testing. A one-on-one test procedure was used to determine the LID threshold. Threshold difference for the tested ChGs can be explained by a presence of the IR absorption lines, a deviation from the glass-composition stoichiometry and their crystallization tendency.

articleTitle: Solitons in SNAP microresonator with various shape
abstract: We investigate the optical frequency comb generation based on axial mode interaction in a cylindrical microresonator with various shapes of effective radius variation. We argue that, regardless of the form of effective radius variation, there will be an anomalous dispersion of group velocities in the system, and therefore a soliton solution will always exist. As an example, we demonstrate the generation of an optical frequency comb in a microcavity with a rectangular radius variation.

articleTitle: Lead-borogermanate glasses co-doped Sm3+/Gd3+ luminescent thermometry materials
abstract: The luminescent properties of co-doped $\mathrm{Sm}^{3+} / \mathbf{G d}^{3+}$ in the $\mathrm{B}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}-\mathrm{GeO}_{2}-\mathrm{PbO}$ glass system were investigated in the temperature range of 423-673 K. Intensity of the $\mathrm{Sm}^{3+}$ band in the range of $525-540 \mathrm{~nm}\left({ }^{4} \mathrm{~F}_{3 / 2} \rightarrow{ }^{6} \mathrm{H}_{5 / 2}\right)$ increased with increasing temperature. The fluorescence intensity ratio (FIR) changes between the thermosensitive band and the band is attributed to transition ${ }^{5} \mathbf{G}_{5 / 2}{ }^{6} \mathbf{H}_{7 / 2}$ was calculated and demonstrated. The results indicate the potential of the synthesized glasses for luminescent thermometry.

articleTitle: Numerical study of a collimated high charge electron beam generation on laser systems with terawatt peak power
abstract: We had numerically studied electron acceleration in the interaction of a terawatt laser pulse with a long-scale target with density approximately $10 \%$ of critical value. Based on PIC simulations, the mechanism of electron acceleration was found to be a combination of direct laser acceleration and laser wakefield acceleration. With the increase in pulse energy, a collimated electron beam with 1 nC charge can be obtained.

articleTitle: Nanosecond tunable from 2 to 3 µm Cr2+: ZnSe solid-state laser
abstract: We developed a tunable in spectral range from 2 to $3 \mu \mathrm{m}$ pulsed solid state laser based on the $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}: \mathrm{ZnSe}^{2}$ crystal with 2.15 mJ maximum output energy at $2.35 \mu \mathrm{m}, 7 \mathrm{~ns}$ pulse length and 100 Hz repetition rate. This laser could be used in theranostic system which combines a laser therapy and optoacoustic diagnoctic.

articleTitle: Integrated Vortex Emitter Design for Mode Signal Multiplexing
abstract: We consider an out-of-plane optical vortex emitter based on an integrated ring resonator, which also multiplexes the emitted vortices in a single optical beam due to using of two access waveguides. One waveguide is phase matched with TE00 ring mode, the other one with TE10 mode. Cylindrical recesses are used as inhomogeneities in the ring, which provides great opportunities to control the radiation efficiency, taking into account the technological limitations of the manufacturing processes. The paper proposes an algorithm for numerical calculation of the geometry of the structure, which makes it possible to determine the width of the ring resonator, its radius, the number of inhomogeneities and their location on the ring, as well as the parameters of the couplers. It is shown that the calculated structures can simultaneously emit two pairs of conjugate vortices at the same wavelength, and the signal of each order can be independently modulated by a useful signal, which determines the prospects for using this device in optical communications, as well as for applications requiring rapid switching of the vortex order in one optical beam.

articleTitle: Fabry-Pérot resonances in a dielectric ring
abstract: A study of the eigenmodes spectrum of a rectangular dielectric ring has been carried out. It is found that the low-frequency spectrum breaks up into separate groups of resonant modes. Linear dependences of the wavelength of resonances on the width and height of the resonator are revealed, representing are Fabry-Perot resonances. The numerical results obtained were confirmed by experiment.

articleTitle: Study of the use of laser radiation with a wavelength of 450 nm to remove pigmented skin formations
abstract: The optimal parameters of laser radiation for the removal and treatment of pigmented skin formations have been determined.

articleTitle: New generation of broad-range femtosecond IR laser sources: the way to multispectral excitation of matter
abstract: Powerful dual-wavelength all-solid-state femtosecond laser complex based on Cr:Forsterite ($1.24 \mu \mathrm{m}$) and $\mathrm{Fe}: \mathrm{ZnSe}(4.6 \mu \mathrm{m})$ crystals allow to create coherent source with multi-band (from VUV to THz) coverage and access to few-cycle pulses. Highly efficient (from $1 \%$ up to $10 \%$) nonlinear conversion of IR pump into spectrally broad waveforms offers opportunities to get insight into matter control by light.

articleTitle: Enhancing the capabilities of generating THz vortices by utilizing advanced spiral zone plates based on carbon nanotubes
abstract: Opticalelements based on nanomaterials have gained significant attention due to their potential for advancing research in the terahertz (THz) region. These materials offer compactness and unique properties such as flexibility and stretchability, which enable precise control of wave beams. In this work, we demonstrate an innovative approach to controlling the THz wavefront using spiral zone plates (SZPs) made of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs). As a demonstration of the concept, we design the SZP using Laguerre-Gauss mode analysis, and subsequently fabricate and experimentally characterize the resulting vortex beams.

articleTitle: Wavelength dependence of transparency current of InGaAs/GaAs quantum well-dot active medium
abstract: We report on the experimental study of the wavelength dependence of transparency current of the novel type of quantum-sized heterostructures - InG aAs/G aA s quantum welldots. Using the obtained results, we have studied the population level of the active region of superluminescent diodes based on chirped quantum well-dot layers and showed that at current density of $160 \mathrm{~A} / \mathrm{cm}^{2}$, the low-energy layer is filled with carriers.

articleTitle: Laser initiated strong THz pulses
abstract: The PIC simulations results on generation of high-energy electron bunch by a short laser pulse propagating in strongly nonlinear relativistic self-trapping regime in a near-critical plasma have been addressed to the production of super-intense THz pulse. It has been demonstrated that a 30 fs 4J laser pulse is able to produce quasi-unipolar Thz pulses with energy of about 100 mJ.

articleTitle: Distributed Strain Sensor Based on Double-Wavelength phi-OTDR
abstract: We propose a new phase recovery approach in a phiOTDR based on weak fiber Bragg gratings (wFBG), utilizing two matched wavelengths. The method and an experimental setup are described. The presented experimental strain measuring results demonstrate an error of less than $5 \mu \mathrm{m}$.

articleTitle: Effect of microenvironment on photophysical properties of Radachlorin photosensitizer
abstract: Variations of major photophysical properties (fluorescence spectrum, quantum yield, lifetime and anisotropy) of the chlorin-e6-based photosensitizer (PS) Radachlorin in solutions were analyzed as a function of such microenvironment properties as acidity, viscosity and polarity, as well as on the presence of albumin molecules. The high affinity of PS molecules to albumins resulted in their uptake by cells via endocytosis and further intracellular transportation by endocytic trafficking with final localization in lysosomes. The intracellular distributions of the PS fluorescence lifetime were shown to correlate with distributions of acidity in cells of five established lines.

articleTitle: Plasmon-enhanced chemiluminescence of lucigenin due to interaction with colloidal gold nanoparticles
abstract: Chemiluminescence enhancement of lucigenin in the vicinity of colloidal gold nanoparticles was studied. The chemiluminescence intensity was found to increase twice independent of the nanoparticle’s concentration in the range of $10^{-4}$ to $10^{-8} \mathrm{M}$.

articleTitle: Polarization singularities in the laser beam self-focusing in liquid crystals isotropic phase near the phase transition temperature
abstract: We consider the appearance and behavior of polarization singularity lines in the process of self-focusing of an elliptically polarized Gaussian beam in an isotropic phase of cholesteric and nematic liquid crystals at a temperature close to the temperature of transition to mesophase. The values of radiation and medium parameters leading to the nucleation of polarization singularities and their unusual behavior are given.

articleTitle: Monitoring optical fiber parameters using stimulated Brillouin scattering
abstract: The effect of the stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) in the optical fibers was experimentally studied. It has been shown that this effect can be used to monitor parameters and early diagnosis of changes in the state of optical fiber. This control method is suitable for DWDM systems.

articleTitle: Self-started tunable femtosecond Cr2+:ZnSe laser from 2.15 to 2.4 μm
abstract: Thisstudy presents the development of a tunable femtosecond laser on a Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>: ZnSe crystal with a Lyot filter in the mid-infrared region. The system provides continuous wavelength tunability in the range of 2.15-2.4 $\mu$m with with a maximum spectrum width of 96.5 nm at a wavelength of 2.2 $\mu$m.

articleTitle: Glass modification by backside irradiation using nano-second laser pulses
abstract: The fiber fuse effect was successfully initiated in various bulk glass materials using backside irradiation with a nanosecond pulsed laser, employing different metallic foils as absorbers. The study reveals unique resultant structures within the glass, which vary depending on the initiation conditions and laser parameters used.

articleTitle: Increasing the sensitivity of spark discharge diagnostics during the transition to the long-wave region
abstract: It was shown that in the laser sensing method, the resolution of the spark channel structure increases during the transition from 532 nm to 1064 nm, which makes it possible to obtain quantitative data on the plasma parameters of a single microchannel.

articleTitle: Picosecond SRS in Water Excited by Bessel Beams
abstract: The process of stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) in water induced by Nd:YAG laser second harmonic picosecond pulses (60 ps) was studied when focusing by a Bessel beam through an open water surface. Generation of two Stokes (650 and 836 nm) and two anti-Stokes (390 and 450 nm) SRS components was obtained. A substantial narrowing of the first Stokes component’s OH band to 75 and $65 \mathrm{~cm}^{-1}$ in backward and forward SRS was observed.

articleTitle: Laser engineering of microbial systems: a new tool for microbiology
abstract: We presents the results related to laser engineering of microbial systems (LIMS) technology, which allows significant progress towards solving the ambitious task of microbiology associated with expanding the base of cultivable microorganisms. The technology is based on laserinduced transfer of microscopic gel droplets with living microorganisms from various natural environments while preserving their natural microenvironment. LIMS is a new promising tool for microbiology, has significant potential for practical applications and is of interest from the point of view of fundamental science about biota.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Higher-order Topological States and Higher-order Topological Solitons
abstract: The topological insulator is new phase of matter that possesses topologically protected one-way edge states that are immune to defects or disorders. Today, the concept of topological insulator has extended to optics and develops rapidly due to its promising potential applications.

articleTitle: Spectral properties of borogermanate glass co-doped with CsPbBr3 nanocrystals and Eu3+ ions
abstract: The spectral properties of borogermanate glass codoped with CsPbBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> perovskite nanocrystals and $\mathrm{Eu}^{3+}$ ions are investigated. Luminescence spectra contain several bands at 600, 615 and 700 nm corresponding to $\mathrm{Eu}^{3+}$ ions and one band in 510535 nm regions dedicated to CsPbBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> nanocrystals. Europium luminescence can be excited through perovskite crystals’ bands.

articleTitle: Bismuth-Doped Heterogeneous Multi-Layered Fibers for Broadband Optical Amplifiers
abstract: A concept of spatial separation of the different types of active centers in a heterogeneous bismuth-doped multilayered fiber design is proposed. This approach can be efficiently used for gain broadening and equalization to achieve wideband amplification in $\mathrm{O}+\mathrm{E}+\mathrm{S}$-band.

articleTitle: 1550-nm VCSELs with p-type active layer doping for improved high-speed performance
abstract: The effect of p-type barrier layer doping in the active region on the modulation speed of a long-wavelength VCSEL is considered. Doping of barrier active region led to an increase in the maximum modulation bandwidth and a decrease in the maximum optical power of the VCSEL.

articleTitle: Quantum-cascade laser with increased ring radius
abstract: The lasing at $7.59 \mu \mathrm{m}$ wavelength was achieved in quantum-cascade surface emitting lasers with increased radius of ring cavity. The large mode number in single-mode spectrum was caused by over coupling between laser core and second-order Bragg grating.

articleTitle: Benchmarking of 8-qudit quantum processor based on optical transition in 171Yb+ ions
abstract: We demonstrate a quantum processor based on a 3D linear Paul trap for 171Y b+ions. The trap design provides high secular frequencies and low heating rate in the radial plane, which together with individual addressing and readout optical systems, allows realization of operations on up to 8 ions in a string. In each of 8 ions, we use four quantum states coupled by the E2 optical transition for qudit encoding, which makes our processor equivalent to a 16 qubit system. We present the results of benchmarking single- and two-qubit operations and realizing basic quantum algorithms, including Bernstein-Vazirani algorithm, Grover search as well as H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and LiH molecular simulations.

articleTitle: Crystal growth and optical properties of TbM3(BO3)4 (M=Al, Ga) crystals
abstract: $\mathrm{TbGa}_{3}\left(\mathrm{BO}_{3}\right)_{4}$ and $\mathrm{TbAl}_{3}\left(\mathrm{BO}_{3}\right)_{4}$ crystals were grown using the $\mathrm{Bi}_{2} \mathrm{Mo}_{3} \mathrm{O}_{12}: \mathrm{B}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}: \mathrm{Tb}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{K}_{2} \mathrm{Mo}_{3} \mathrm{O}_{10}: \mathrm{B}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}: \mathrm{Tb}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}$ flux, respectively. The produced compounds crystallize in the R32 space group. A strong green emission of the luminescence is primarily dominated by the ${ }^{5} \mathrm{D}_{4}$ to ${ }^{7} F_{5}$ transition in $\mathrm{Tb}^{3+}$. According to the data obtained, the SHG efficiency is higher for the $\mathrm{TbGa}_{3}\left(\mathrm{BO}_{3}\right)_{4}$ compound due to its higher molar mass.

articleTitle: The dynamics of laser generation in single-mode semiconductor (1060 nm) emitters microbar under sub-ns pulse pumping
abstract: The operation of single-mode semiconductor (1060 nm) emitters microbar without optical coupling between the stripes was studied. The operation in the regime of a single relaxation optical pulse with a duration of 140 ps and power up to 3 W was demonstrated. The beam diagram of the microbar corresponded to the pattern of a single-mode emitter.

articleTitle: The trajectory of the propogation of oblique rays in optical fibers with a stepped profile of the reflective index
abstract: The paper describes the latest results on the calculation of the trajectories of the propagation of oblique rays in optical fibers. One of the options is three-dimensional, which consists in sequentially calculating the coordinates of the points of ray reflections in vector form. The second option is twodimensional, it consists in calculating the transverse coordinates for the reflection pointso.

articleTitle: Quantum Yield of Bismuth Active Centers Luminescence in Germanosilicate Optical Fibers
abstract: The quantum yield (QY) of luminescence of bismuth active centers associated with silica (BAC-Si) in bismuthdoped optical fibers was measured. The luminescence bands peaked at 830 nm and 1400 nm were excited at $800 \mathrm{~nm}, 1240 \mathrm{~nm}$ and 1310 nm. The branching ratio (BR) of radiative transitions at 830 nm and 1400 nm excited at 800 nm was defined. The influence of co-doping with boron on QY and BR is examined.

articleTitle: Highly transient Raman convertion in SrMoO4 under ultrafast double-pulse pumping
abstract: Highly transient stimulated Raman scattering in a SrMoO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> crystal on both stretching (888cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>) and bending (327cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>) Raman modes under ultrafast double-pulse pumping by orthogonally polarized pump pulses at 1030 nm with a controllable chirp and a different delay between them was investigated.

articleTitle: Robust Launching of Soliton Molecules in a Hybrid Mode-Locked Er-Doped Fiber Laser
abstract: The effective launch of low-noise soliton molecules was obtained using newly developed partially-ordered densely packed single-walled carbon nanotubes in a hybrid scheme of an Er-doped ultrashort pulse fiber laser.

articleTitle: Quantum electrodynamics cascade arising at reflection of a multipetawatt laser pulse from a solid plasma target
abstract: Quantum electrodynamics (QED) cascade arising in a superposition of incident multipetawatt laser pulse and its reflection from a solid target were studied numerically and analytically.

articleTitle: Spectroscopy investigation of highly doped LiCaAlF6:Ce3+ crystals
abstract: Crystals of the UV lasers active media $\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}: \mathrm{LiCaAlF}_{6}$, which are characterized by the formation of several types of $\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}$ ion centers, have been studied. Presence of nonequivalent impurity centers was confirmed by detection of zero-phonon lines for two centers in low-temperature luminescence spectra, as well as from EPR spectra for various magnetic field orientations relative to the crystallographic axes of the samples. We have shown that for $\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}: \mathrm{LiCaAlF}_{6}$ crystals, with an increase in the concentration of $\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}$ ions in the melt, crystallization occurs in such a way that the concentration of impurity centers of lower symmetry increases to a greater extent than centers of higher symmetry. Moreover, laser oscillation belongs to precisely this type of center.

articleTitle: Features of high-order soliton molecule amplification in an Er-doped fiber amplifier
abstract: We report on the generation and amplification of soliton molecule regime in master oscillator fiber amplifier based on erbium-doped fiber laser. The amplification of 15 pulses regime with 432 fs pulses duration and 46 mW average power in 1m long erbium-doped fiber amplifier led to the generation of 20 pulses regime with 449 fs pulses duration and 102 mW average power.

articleTitle: Influence of Fe2+-co-doping on Cr2+ ion spectroscopic properties in Zn0.7Mn0.3Se and Zn0.7Mg0.3Se crystals at room-temperature
abstract: The influence of $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ co-doping on the spectroscopic properties of $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ ions in $\mathrm{Zn}_{1-x} \mathrm{Mn}_{\mathrm{x}} \mathrm{Se}$ and Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> ${ }_{\mathrm{x}} \mathrm{Mg}_{\mathrm{x}} \mathrm{Se}(\mathrm{x}=0.3$) crystals at room temperature is demonstrated. The absorption and fluorescence peak wavelengths shift to higher energies in the Cr -Fe co-doped crystals. The fluorescence decay curves in the Cr -Fe co-doped crystals have a non-exponential shape with the same lifetimes at the far stage as the crystals doped only with $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$.

articleTitle: Robot-assisted photodynamic therapy
abstract: Medical robot assisted fluorescence diagnostics (FD) and photodynamic therapy (PDT) of malignant lesions of external localizations, as well as intraoperative PDT is presented. This technique provides accuracy and uniformity of laser radiation distribution on the object and safety of treatment protocol.

articleTitle: Holographic Interferometers for Optical Digital Medical Tomography
abstract: The report presents a recent achievements in holographic interferometry for digital optical tomographs used in biomedical applications. The most common practical techniques are considered: sample rotating, single-shot, phase-shifting, and the technique adaptive holographic interferometers. Estimates of technical parameters are given and the advantages and disadvantages of various schemes. The basic concepts of angular and phase coding of the studied objects are given.

articleTitle: Toroidal and cruciform vector laser solitons and their transformations
abstract: We predict a new type of 3D optical dissipative vector solitons in a homogeneous isotropic medium with laser amplification and saturable absorption. Both circular polarization components have the toroidal intensity distribution and a unit topological charge. Soliton properties and polarization structure depend on the angle between toroidal circular components.

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental study of the effect of laser heating on the optical characteristics of human skin
abstract: The results of a theoretical and experimental study of the effect of laser heating on the optical characteristics of human skin are discussed. For the first time in an in vivo experiment, the dependence of the reflectance spectrum of human skin when heated by laser radiation with a wavelength of 980 nm was measured. Within the framework of a numerical seven-layer optical computer model of human skin, an interpretation of the experimental results is given, and it is shown that the change in reflectance observed in the experiment may be associated with the conversion of skin blood hemoglobin into methemoglobin.

articleTitle: Luminescence temperature sensing based on spectral characteristic of CeF3-TbF3-YF3 nanoparticles
abstract: When $\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}$ ions are excited, intense peaks of luminescence of $\mathbf{T b}^{3+}$ ions are observed, which indicates an obvious energy transfer from $\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}$ to $\mathrm{Tb}^{3+}$. It has been shown that the ratio of the intensities of the luminescence bands $\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}$ to $\mathbf{T b}^{3+}$ is a decreasing function depending on temperature. The ratio of the intensities of the luminescence bands of $\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}$ and $\mathrm{Tb}^{3+}$ ions (in the range of $303-523 \mathrm{~K}$) was used as a temperature-dependent parameter. The rate of decrease in the LIR function decreases with increasing temperature for different concentrations of $\mathbf{T b}^{\mathbf{3 +}}$ ions. It has been suggested that this phenomenon is due to the presence of two processes populating the ${ }^{5} \mathrm{D}_{4}$ state of the $\mathbf{T b}^{3+}$ ion. There are a multiphonon non-radiation transition from the ${ }^{5} D_{3}$ to ${ }^{5} D_{4}$ level of the $\mathbf{T b}^{3+}$ ion (more temperature-dependent) and cross-relaxation between $\mathbf{T b}^{3+}$ ions, which was estimated as less temperature-dependent process.

articleTitle: Particle drift, diffusion, and acceleration in quasi-static fields generated by ultrashort relativistically intense laser pulse channeling in near-critical density targets
abstract: The dynamics of charged particles in the self-generated quasistatic fields of channels produced by the interaction of an ultrashort relativistically intense laser pulse with near-critical density plasmas has been studied numerically and analytically. We identify distinctive mechanisms of drift, diffusion, and acceleration of electrons in quasi-static fields generated in the laser plasma channel produced by ultrashort intense laser pulses.

Author Keywords: interaction of an intense laser pulse with a near-critical-density plasma

articleTitle: Emission induced by an energy transfer from electronic excitations in SiO2 to N2 molecules
abstract: For the first time, an emission induced by an energy transfer from electronic excitations in SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> to N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> molecules surrounding SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sample is observed. The emission is found both in the cases of a single-crystalline and a highly-dispersed SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Electronic excitations were created in SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> by the two-photon absorption of laser radiation at 205 nm and by the bombardment with a high-current electron beam with the average particle energy of 150 keV. A presumable qualitative model of energy transfer at the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> surface is suggested.

articleTitle: Enhancement of nuclear reaction yield in nano–structure targets irradiated by circular polarized, ultrashort and intense laser pulses
abstract: We consider effective production of nuclear reactions in nano-structure target irradiated by circular polarized, intense, ultrashort laser pulses. The optimal for strong magnetic fields laser and target parameters were found by the analytical modelling and three dimensional particles in cell simulations. It is shown that such fields slow down the structure expansion, which significantly enhances nuclear reaction yield.

articleTitle: Novel oxochloride lead silicate glass doped with neodimium ions for NIR applications
abstract: Nd-doped lead oxochloride silicate glasses were synthesized and their spectral characteristics were studied. The new synthesis technique made it possible to reduce losses due to lead chloride volatilization to two mass percent. Based on the combination of physical and chemical characteristics, these materials are promising for photonics and fiber optics applications.

articleTitle: New materials for photodynamic inactivation of viruses
abstract: The studies carried out in this work on the effective generation of singlet oxygen in the volume and on the surface of polytetrafluoroethylene (fluoroplastic-4, also known under the trade mark as Teflon) when irradiated with ultraviolet and visible radiation made it possible to clarify the mechanisms and features of the antiviral action of this fluoropolymer under specific experimental conditions.

articleTitle: 1 MW Peak Power Tapered Fiber Amplifier of Picosecond Pulses Operated near 1030 nm
abstract: Inthe present work, the tapered Yb-doped fiber amplifier was optimized for operation in the spectral range near 1030 nm. Stimulated Raman scattering and four-wave mixing were nonlinear effects that limited the power scaling. We determined a superior gain regime, taper configuration, and pump injection condition to maximize the threshold of these nonlinear effects. As a result, we obtained two operating regimes: 13 ps pulses were amplified to 670 kW peak and 39 W average power in the first case, and to 1 MW peak and 13.8 MW average power in the second case. The fraction of unwanted components in the output spectrum did not exceed 2.5%, and the beam quality was almost diffraction-limited $\left(\mathrm{M}^{2}\lt 1.2\right)$.

articleTitle: Aluminum metasurface as a booster for chemiluminescence sensors
abstract: Chemiluminescence, notwithstanding its relatively low yield, is an important transduction mechanism for chemical and biological sensors. To extend the applicability of chemiluminescence sensors in more demanding situations we explore the opportunity to enhance the chemiluminescence intensity via acceleration of radiation transitions which is known to be possible in the vicinity of a periodic array of metal nanoparticles possessing localized surface plasmon resonances. The results of a global search of the best parameters are presented.

articleTitle: Temperature-induced distortions redistribution of the stacked-actuator deformable mirrors with various apertures under different cooling regimes
abstract: In this paper the behavior of the stacked-actuator deformable mirrors with various apertures under high-power laser radiation with 10 kW power was simulated with finite element method. Thermomechanical analysis of the wavefront corrector was performed in three main cases: without thermostabilization, cooling through actuators body and with applying periphery thermostabilization. The simulation results showed that the best cooling of deformable mirrors is achieved with heat dissipation along the periphery of the mirror substrate.

articleTitle: Increasing the average and peak power of thin slab based laser amplifier
abstract: We developed Yb:YAG thin slab scalable laser amplifier and investigated numerically and experimentally the main problems limiting its average and peak power: overheating, surface breakdown and pump power scaling. We have shown that using composite gradient doped slab with compensation of beam area compression effect allows to use pump power to 1000 W with maximum output energy of 50 mJ with a M2<1.5.

articleTitle: Temperature dependence of the pump radiation transfer efficiency in side-pumped optical fibers
abstract: A method for measuring temperature dependence of optical radiation transfer coefficients between two waveguides in the DSCCP (Distributed side-coupled cladding-pumped fiber) fiber has been developed. Proposed technique significantly increases the speed and accuracy of measurements. Obtained results allow to find the optimal polymer composition for fiber coating in high-power fiber lasers.

articleTitle: Pb-catalyzed GaAs nanowires grown by molecular beam epitaxy on Si substrate
abstract: For n-type doping of A3B5 semiconductors silicon are commonly used. However, Si in A3B5 nanowire is p-type dopant. Species are incorporated into nanowire through the intermediate liquid phase. Solubility of metals in catalyst are usually much more than nitrogen family elements. Nitrogen family elements easily dissolve in metal carbon family elements such as lead and tin. Here we discuss the growth of GaAs nanowires with lead catalyst on Si substrate. Lead could easily dissolve nitrogen family elements as well as boron family elements, which allows to switch nanowire growth from metal-rich to pnictide-rich growth.

articleTitle: Development of biosensors based on surface plasmon resonance imaging technique
abstract: The work is devoted to the development of a biosensor based on the phenomenon of surface plasmon resonance. In the process of the work, multiple measurements were carried out at the SPRi facility. The parameters such as sensitivity of the method and resolution limit were also evaluated. The values of these parameters were found to be comparable to the sensitivity and resolution of the frustrated total internal reflection method.

articleTitle: Determination of gold concentration in colloids by UV-vis spectroscopy: universality for various nanoparticles and clusters
abstract: The UV-vis method is applied to six experimental and theoretical Au models: nanosphere particles and clusters, nanorods, 2D nanotriangles and nanoplates, and 3D nanostars. We fabricated 34 samples with different nanoparticle sizes, shapes, morphology, and Au concentrations. From simulated and experimental data, we derived a universal relation between gold concentration and extinction at $400 \mathrm{~nm}[\mathrm{Au0}](\mathrm{mM})=0.44 \times \mathrm{A}_{400}$.

articleTitle: Multilayer interference metamaterials for advancing THz-TDS technique
abstract: Here we present the design of multilayer interference metamaterials that provide high-performance, terahertz quasi-optical bandpass and cutoff filters made on their basis. The filters help us to implement antialias filtering and subsampling (undersampling) methods in the terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) technique. It is shown that the proposed approaches can significantly reduce the data acquisition time of the spectrometer, which in turn can speed up terahertz vision systems built on the basis of THz-TDS.

articleTitle: Numerical calculation of arranged-microvoid volumetric reflective gratings in ZnSe
abstract: In this paper, we performed a numerical calculation of arranged-microvoid volumetric reflective gratings in ZnSe crystal. These volumetric modifications are prospective to be used instead of reflective coatings in miniaturized lasers. The calculation results revealed the effectiveness of the proposed method compared to multilayer reflective coatings.

articleTitle: An OFDR’s hardware and software optimization and its performance estimation
abstract: In this work, we describe an optical frequency domain reflectometer (OFDR) where the gas cell channel and the auxiliary interferometer are combined into one channel. Data from this channel is extracted using empirical mode decomposition and frequency filtering. With this method we identify events on the trace without loss of quality. The proposed solution makes OFDRs cheaper and smaller.

articleTitle: Method of deep joint formation at laser welding of biological tissues
abstract: A new method of weld irradiation in the process of laser soldering of biological tissues is proposed. The method will allow transporting laser radiation to the area of weld formation with fewer losses, which allows minimizing the formation of temperature necrosis of the tissue. Modelling has shown the possibility of forming deeper welds compared to stationary irradiation methods, with a slight increase in the area of thermal necrosis of the joined tissues.

articleTitle: Influence of fluid microstructure on dynamics of laser-induced post-effects
abstract: We studied the evolution of shock waves and cavitation bubbles generated by femto- and nanosecond laser pulses over a time scale ranging from femtoseconds to microseconds in various molecular environments, including supercritical states. Through time-resolved shadow photography techniques, we observed that when highly intense laser pulses are focused into a supercritical fluid like carbon dioxide, cavitation bubbles do not collapse as in liquid media. Instead, clusters ranging from 1 to 200 microns in size are formed, presenting a significant differnce from the typical dynamics of cavitation bubbles induced by laser in liquids which exhibit size fluctuations

articleTitle: Direct observation of stimulated emission of NV– centers in synthetic HPHT diamond
abstract: Data on direct observation of stimulated emission of $\mathrm{NV}^{-}$centres in synthetic NRNT-diamonds located in a focused pump beam are presented. The spectra and pulse durations of the stimulated emission were simultaneously recorded. It was found that the shapes of the spectra and the intensity of stimulated emission depend on the number of emitting centres and the position of the crystal relative to the focus of the pump beam.

articleTitle: Production of hybrid materials in the MF2 (M=Ba,Ca):Liq system by co-precipitation
abstract: Hybridmaterials were obtained in the MF2 matrices (M=Ba, Ca) using an organic phosphor lithium (8-hydroxyquinolate). Hybrid materials were obtained by direct and reverse co-precipitation from aqueous-alcoholic solutions with ammonium fluoride under various synthesis conditions. The dependence of the photoluminescence intensity on the organic phosphor content was studied. The resulting luminescent materials have effective broadband photoluminescence in the region of 390-650nm.

IEEE Keywords: Active matrix organic light emitting diodes

articleTitle: Quantum ghost polarimetry with correlated photons
abstract: In this work, a theory of quantum ghost polarimetry in the post-selection regime is proposed. Twodimensional ghost images of polarized objects using correlated photons were experimentally obtained.

articleTitle: Gas Lasers Based on Hollow-Core Fibers
abstract: Progress in the development of gas lasers that are based on hollow-core fibers is reviewed. Gas fiber lasers based on both population inversion and stimulated Raman scattering are considered. Recent demonstration of the first gas-discharge fiber laser is discussed.

articleTitle: Laser-pumping attack on QKD sources
abstract: For the first time, we demonstrate a new type of attack on QKD systems based on laser pumping of a photon source. It includes injection of cw laser emission into a source at a wavelength that shorter than the system operating one. Particularly, we show that laser emission at 1310 nm induces increase in photon number at 1550 nm, changes in pulse shape and width. The QKD risk evaluation due to laser-pumping attack is presented.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic hot spots in dielectric cylindrical and ring resonators
abstract: The results of theoretical and experimental study of photonic resonances accompanied by the appearance of electromagnetic hot spots in subwavelength dielectric ring resonators and cylinder-ring dimers are presented. An intense electric hot spot appears in the small central hole at the topological transition from a cylinder to a ring only for eigenmodes with azimuthal number $m=1$, which follows from Mie theory. For a large central hole, if a smaller cylinder is placed inside it, a hot spot at multiple resonance frequencies is observed in the gap between two objects.

articleTitle: Switching platform for writing/erasing laser-induced periodic surface structures (LIPSS) on GST
abstract: A switching platform that provides writing and erasing of extended two-phase periodic laser-induced surface structures on the GST has been developed: writing is carried out by fs laser pulses, and erasing - by electric current ones. The obtained results demonstrated the possibility of using a thin-film resistive heating element of the developed design to create elements of non-volatile active integrated optical and optoelectronic devices, for example, tunable diffraction gratings.

articleTitle: Dark-state resonances in elliptically polarized field for alkali-metal vapors in a buffer-gas cell
abstract: We investigate dark-state resonances for alkali-metal atoms in a cell with buffer gases excited by frequency modulated elliptically polarized laser field. It is shown that all the resonance parameters depend on the ellipticity and that for some parameters this dependence is crucial for designing high-performance chip-scale atomic clocks.

articleTitle: High-brilliance synchrotron radiation in relativistic self-trapping regime
abstract: Synchrotron radiation source based on the laser-plasma acceleration of electrons in the relativistic self-trapping regime of the laser pulse propagation has a small size, short duration and low divergence that provides a high brightness. We discuss angular-spectral characteristics of this secondary radiation, which can be generated using the high-power laser facilities that already exist or are under construction in Russia.

articleTitle: Feasibility of Photodynamic Effect Assessment by means of Microcirculation Optical Monitoring During Laser Activation
abstract: Assessment of the skin microcirculation during photoactivation is in demand for studying photodynamic therapy mechanisms and, based on this, increasing its effectiveness and safety. Most of conventional non-invasive in vivo methods for diagnosing the vascular network in the skin upper layers do not implement monitoring directly during photoactivation. The study was aimed at evaluating the feasibility of monitoring early changes in skin microcirculation during photoactivation using videocapillaroscopy and photoplethysmography. We proposed an approach, designed its hardware and software, and approved it when studying the response of skin microcirculation in rats under various modes of laser activation with low power density. Analysis of the data acquired by the designed setup revealed differences in the microcirculation response to such treatment. Specifically, there was a discrepancy in the time periods between the exposure onset, the blood flow lacks and the beginning of the recovery period, as well as in the duration of the latter. The proposed approach ensured non-invasive vessel imaging and blood perfusion quantifying continuously during laser activation, and may complement general methods for investigation of functional principles of the microcirculation response to photodynamic therapy.

articleTitle: Refractive phase masks for lensless laser beam shaping
abstract: This work describes a method of laser beam transformation in lensless optical systems by phase SLM. This method relies on an iterative algorithm of wavefront reconstruction that uses a physical model of back propagation of a conjugated wave front and smooth morphing of the target beam profile, also avoiding Fourier transform in calculations and therefore lenses in the optical system. It allows designing refractive phase masks that produce a smooth wavefront. This method allows practically arbitrary beam transformation, including formation of beams with a smooth phase and intensity profiles, thus solving the problem of pixel-to-pixel matching when using SLM in a doublepass configuration that usually arises when using diffractive phase masks.

articleTitle: Formation of nanovoids grating in Zr/SiO2/Si at scanning of tightly focused cw laser beam
abstract: The formation of nanovoid grating at thermochemical laser writing on $\mathrm{Zr} / \mathrm{SiO}_{2} / \mathrm{Si}$ multi-layer material has been demonstrated. Unlike other publications, continuous rather than pulsed laser radiation was used in this work. Possible mechanism of the effect is discussed.

articleTitle: Frequency and Intensity Noise Measurement of Single-Frequency Lasers
abstract: We report the results of frequency and intensity noise measurements of single-frequency lasers. Different types of semiconductor and fiber lasers were investigated. RF phase noise analyzer was used to measure the frequency noise of beat notes of the lasers. The fiber lasers have the lowest frequency noise and at the same time high values of the relative intensity noise.

articleTitle: Luminescence features of heteronanostructures passivated by layers of colloidal quantum dots under intense laser excitation
abstract: The photoluminescence of nanostructures in the form InP/InAsP/InP nanowires, passivated by layers of colloidal $\mathrm{CdSe} / \mathrm{ZnS}$ quantum dots at increasing pump power, has been studied. A feature of the system is the existence of several luminescent centers connected through mechanisms of multi-stage non-radiative excitation transfer. It has been shown that the kinetics of decay of excited states depends on the nature of excitation. The effects of ‘filling exciton states” and “delayed confinement effect” are discussed

articleTitle: Targeted PLGA nanoparticles as versatile platfrom for the delivery of oncotherapeutic compounds
abstract: The advancement of techniques for non-invasive targeted chemotherapy is one of the most important directions in contemporary oncology. Polymer nanoparticles based on poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) and loaded with diagnostic and oncotherapeutic substances show immense potential as tools for cancer diagnosis and treatment. In this study, we present the creation of targeted polymer nanoparticles, targosomes, which are loaded with paclitaxel for imaging and treatment of HER2-positive cancer. These synthesized nanoparticles were employed for targeted delivery to tumors and tumor growth reduction in vivo.

articleTitle: Adapting laser microscopy to life sciences
abstract: Transmission, scattering and fluorescence microscopy are adapted to various requirements of life sciences, e.g. 3D resolution and limitation of light exposure to a nonphototoxic level. Applications include super-resolution microscopy and laser-assisted micromanipulation.

articleTitle: Classification of Acoustic Influences with phi-OTDR Using Trace Pattern Recognition
abstract: In this study, we propose a new approach to solve the problem of binary classifying acoustic impacts recorded with a phi-OTDR that have low SNR. The first model is used to extract spatial features, the second is used to extract temporal dependencies. Ensembled models that extract spatial and time features is an effective solution to overcome some of each other’s imperfections. Stacking was used as an ensemble technique. The accuracy of predictions on the test sample for confirmed alarms was 97.18% and 97.43% for false alarms.

articleTitle: Luminescent properties of the Er3+/Yb3+co-doped Bi2O3-GeO2 glasses
abstract: Erbium and ytterbium co-doped bismuth-germanate glasses were synthesized and their luminescent characteristics have been investigated. It was shown that addition of these rare-earth oxides leads to an expansion of the luminescence spectral range of $\mathrm{Bi}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}-\mathrm{GeO}_{2}$ glasses.

articleTitle: Laser-Induced Singlet Oxygen Stimuates Bioenergetics of Insulin-Producing Cells
abstract: The paper presents the results of the study of the effect of singlet oxygen induced by 1267 nm laser irradiation without the use of photosensitizers on the bioenergetics of rat RINm5F insulinoma cells.

articleTitle: Optical radiation homogeniser of a power supply system with energy transfer via optical fibre
abstract: The paper proposes a power supply system with power transmission via optical fiber. The research on optimization of the optical path design is carried out. Modeling is performed in the geometrical optics module of the COMSOL Multiphysics software package by the finite element method. A digital model of a homogenizer for a photovoltaic converter (PVC) was obtained.

articleTitle: Simple method for spherical aberration correction in direct laser writing.
abstract: The relation is established which shows the focussing depths with compensated spherical aberrations under the high aperture focussing through the planar surface in materials with different refractive indices and the same pre-compensation settings in focussing optics. Typically, the focussing objective possesses the correction ring calibrated for single specific material. The developed relation allows calculation of depth at which correct pre-compensation is applied for any material.

articleTitle: Clarification of data on phase states in the Zn-Te-O system
abstract: In this work, the cross section of the phase diagram of the Zn-Te-O system at a temperature of 823 K was clarified experimentally using the high-temperature equilibrium quenching method. During the work, the T-x cross section was studied within the chosen temperature and 6 monovariant equilibria were clarified. It has been demonstrated that the Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf> compound is shifted to the region of oxygen deficiency. Fundamental research was carried out using high-purity reagents, which eliminates the influence of impurity elements on the phase equilibria under study.

articleTitle: Yellow neon laser pumped by a pulsed inductive longitudinal discharge
abstract: The experimental studies results of the energy, temporal and spatial lasing characteristics of Penning neon laser ($\lambda=585.3 \mathrm{~nm}$) pumped by a pulsed inductive longitudinal discharge are presented. The maximum generation energy of 0.14 mJ was obtained in a mixture of $\mathrm{Ne}: \mathrm{H}_{2}-1: 2$. Lasing power reached 700 W with average radiation pulses durations of 200 ns (FWHM). The divergence of the laser beam was no more than 2 mrad.

articleTitle: Diagnostics of plasma channel parameters by optical plasma radiation in laser-plasma electron acceleration experiment
abstract: A method for plasma channel characterization by optical plasma radiation was developed. The electron density of the unperturbed plasma was obtained from the backward stimulated Raman scattering spectrum, and the phase velocity of laser pulse inside the plasma channel was calculated from the second harmonic radiation angle.

articleTitle: Ir(III) complexes – sensors for hypoxia detection
abstract: In this work we report the design, synthesis and implementation of novel iridium(III) O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensors in bioimaging.

articleTitle: Investigation of solid solutions of Eu3+-doped CaxNa(1-x)/2Gd(1-x)/2MoO4 (x = 0 - 1) crystals
abstract: The single crystals of the concentration series of $\mathrm{CaMoO}_{4}-\mathrm{Na}_{0.5} \mathrm{Gd}_{0.5} \mathbf{M o O}_{4}$ scheelite-like solid solutions was grown and investigated. According to most of the properties studied, this solid solution shows some deviations from additivity.

articleTitle: Hidden Photon Detection
abstract: An experiment is proposed to search for hidden photons generated in nonlinear interactions in a dielectric medium.

articleTitle: Simulation of super-Gaussian laser beam propagation over 1 km turbulent atmospheric path with account for pre-generated Kolmogorov phase screens
abstract: The turbulence simulator software that generates the sequence of phase screens with Kolmogorov spectra is developed and tested. The numerical experiment of laser beam propagation over the 1 km horizontal turbulent atmospheric path is performed and results are investigated.

articleTitle: Research of ultrashort laser processing Si and glass for microelectronics applications
abstract: Research of the laser processing by femtosecond pulses of borosilicate glass and silicon substrate has been carried out. The parameters of laser radiation to minimize the degree of impact on the silicon substrate are determined. At pulse energies in the range from 11 to $15 \mu \mathrm{J}$, a weld is formed at the interface “glass-silicon substrate”. Experiments were carried out on laser cutting of glass to form a base cut. The work of perforating holes in the glass-silicon connection was completed, and the chips were cut with a laser with minimal exposure to the temperature front.

articleTitle: Extreme events in dynamics of frequency-swept semiconductor lasers
abstract: We numerically model a frequency-swept shortcavity semiconductor laser and report the appearance of extreme events in its dynamics. These events, with probability strictly dependent on the sweep rate, appear as a jump from the isola of periodic solutions to the stable region of the bridge periodic solutions and exhibit a high degree of localization.

articleTitle: Four-frequency Zeeman laser gyroscopes with a symmetrical cavity, a system for separating rotation signals from orthogonal polarizations and a perimeter control system
abstract: This paper presents four-frequency Zeeman laser gyroscopes with a cavity in the form of an isohedral and regular tetrahedrons. Optical or mathematical and electronical methods were used to separate the beat signals of counterpropagating waves of orthogonal polarization. Perimeter control system uses the signal of co-directional waves’ beats. A significant suppression of the external magnetic fields influence was shown.

articleTitle: Annealing of lead thin films on silicon
abstract: III-arsenide nanowires are often grown via the vapor-liquid-solid mechanism with foreign catalyst. Here we discuss the initial stage of nanowire growth with tin and lead catalyst - annealing of thin film. The influence of temperature and time of annealing was discussed.

articleTitle: Luminescent characteristics of neodymium-doped oxochloride lead-borate glasses
abstract: Thespectral-luminescent characteristics of oxochloride lead-borate glasses doped NdF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> are investigated. Two concentration series of these glasses were studied - for lead chloride (up to $40 \mathrm{~mol} \%$) and neodymium fluoride (up to 2 $\mathrm{mol} \%)$.

articleTitle: Enhancement of magnetic dipole emission in the presence of a spherical particle
abstract: We discover regimes for promoting fluorescence of magnetic light by four orders of magnitude due to magnetic dipole (MD) transitions of trivalent rare-earth ions $\mathrm{Eu}^{3+}$ located inside or near dielectric homogeneous spheres. A number of configurations, including sphere parameters and the radial position of the rare-earth emitter, at which the transition coupling coefficient approaches the limit value $\approx 1$, which means that the transitions from a given level are completely dominated by the MD transition, have been determined. We present configurations for which the directivity of the resultant emission can be larger than 25.

articleTitle: A method for creating a metasurface based on titanium dioxide
abstract: This paper demonstrates a method for creating metasurfaces based on titanium dioxide, which can be used to design photosensitive elements capable of converting solar energy into electricity. This is possible due to the developed method, which allows you to form a surface with a given frequency. The introduction of metallic nanoparticles into the titanium dioxide matrix makes it possible to enhance the absorption effect of the visible radiation spectrum, and linear carbon chains provide electronic transport over the surface.

articleTitle: Multifunctional Hybrid Nanoparticles as Vectors for Regulating the Expression of Target Genes
abstract: The study focuses on developing multifunctional hybrid nanoparticles for gene therapy and addresses the need for carriers of minimal cytotoxicity. The obtained nanoparticles exhibit optical and superparamagnetic properties, biomolecule binding, form stable complexes with therapeutic nucleic acids, and can serve as carriers for gene regulation. They demonstrate high efficiency in targeted siRNA delivery and offer biocompatibility and potential for controlled intracellular applications.

articleTitle: Portable Optoelectronic Vibration Sensor Based on Self-Mixing Effect in a Laser Diode
abstract: Optoelectronic vibration sensors represent an innovative solution in the field of remote vibration diagnostics. In this work, the sensor is developed that for vibration diagnostics and obtaining in real time the vibration parameters of a remote object, i.e., vibration displacement, vibration velocity and vibration acceleration. A distinctive feature of the proposed technique is the autodyne effect in diode lasers, which allows to generate a probe signal and detect a vibration signal using a single optoelectronic device, a laser diode. An experimental realization of the sensor allowed the vibration parameter measurement with a relative error of 10% at distances up to 500 mm and the vibration frequency range from 20 to 500 Hz.

articleTitle: In-well pumping of an InGaP/AlGaInP-based semiconductor disk laser
abstract: Semiconductor disk laser based on the InGaP/AlGaInP heterostructure, emitting at λ = 645 nm, was studied under in-well pumping by a pulsed ~1-μs dye laser. The pulse power of 72 W with slope efficiency of 17 % were achieved.

Author Keywords: vertical external cavity surface emitting laser (VECSEL)

articleTitle: Temperature stabilized microfluidic chip for plasmonic fiber biosensor
abstract: Here, we present experimental realization of plasmonic fiber biosensor incorporated in microfluidic chip with thermostabilization. The fiber biosensor was based on a tilted fiber Bragg grating covered with a thin gold layer to generate surface plasmon resonance. Temperature stabilization was realized by implementation of a Peltier cell with active PID-controller to exclude the influence of temperature changes in the measured medium. Furthermore, the plasmonic surface of fiber was functionalized with specific proteins to selectively detect biomarkers in biofluids. Marker detection is achieved through a change in the refractive index due to the specific reaction of the interaction of specific proteins with biomarkers on the surface of the optical fiber.

articleTitle: Comparison of SERS spectra of intact and inactivated viruses via machine learning algorithms for the viral disease’s diagnosis application
abstract: This study explores using inactivated influenza A viruses instead of intact ones for creating a spectral database in a diagnostic method with SERS and machine learning. Spectral differences between the forms reveal limitations in using inactivated viruses for database creation and ML training for virus detection, but the data obtained can be utilized for vaccine quality monitoring technology.

articleTitle: Kilowatt-class multi-element first cladding fiber laser
abstract: The article presents the results on experimental elaboration of a fiber laser technology with multi-element first cladding (MFC) manufactured at RFNC - VNIITF. A mockup of ytterbium single-mode fiber laser of 1000 W maximum output power has been designed and implemented. The obtained results will allow updating requirements to the MFC laser produced and further increasing output power and reliability of such lasers.

articleTitle: Holmium Fiber Laser Generation Switching Using Excited State Absorption
abstract: We have demonstrated optical switching of generation in the Holmium-doped fiber laser. The generation switching from continuous-wave to pulsed regime was performed by external pulsed radiation with a wavelength of $\approx 1.6 \mu \mathrm{m}$ due to excited state absorption from ${ }^{5} I_{7}$ level.

articleTitle: Interferometric Studies of Nanoparticle Conjugates for Ultrasensitive Detection of Zearalenone in Food
abstract: Zearalenone (ZEA) is a mycotoxin, a contaminant of agricultural products that has a negative effect on the immune system of both humans and animals. The kinetics of the interaction of conjugates of bovine serum albumin ZEA with monoclonal antibodies against ZEA and functionalized nanometers was characterized using a low-coherence interferometric setup. An ultra-sensitive approach has been developed for the determination of ZEA in food products at the place of demand based on characterized conjugates in combination with highly sensitive electronic registration of magnetic nanometers by nonlinear magnetization. Detection limits in $\mathrm{pg} / \mathrm{ml}$ units are achieved using covalently immobilized magnetic tags and are slightly higher with non-covalent antibody sorption.

articleTitle: Lattice dynamics of Si under intense laser impact
abstract: Using time-resolved techniques we revealed the dynamics of Si lattice under impact of intense nanosecond and femtosecond laser pulse. The energy transfer from laser-induced plasma to the atomic subsystem occurs on a sub-ps timescale, generates a shock wave that leads to the cascade of phase transitions (Si-X => Si-VII => Si-VI => Si-XI => Si-XII=>Si-III).

articleTitle: Modeling the Propagation of Laguerre-Gaussian Beams Through a Turbulent Medium
abstract: This work investigates the influence of atmospheric turbulence on Laguerre-Gaussian modes of various orders. Turbulence is modeled using special phase masks and spatial light modulator. The selection of the optimal mode is carried out by analyzing the drop in the signal-to-noise ratio at the output

articleTitle: Stochastic narrowband generation in a random fiber Raman laser
abstract: Just above the generation threshold the spectrum of a random fiber laser consists of ultra-narrow localized modes, which evolve for time intervals of about 1 ms and decompose afterwards. We characterize its main features: lifetimes and power of these modes, their temporal and statistical properties and articulate the mechanism of modes’ decay as a nonlinear wave mixing process.

articleTitle: Theoretical research of the spectral absorption line broadening in the development of K DPAL
abstract: The results of computational and theoretical studies of diode-pumped alkali laser parameters are presented. Calculation of the absorption spectral line profile for potassium at different parameters of the active medium was performed. At a buffer gas pressure of ${ }^{4} \mathrm{He}$ above 0.1 atm., the greatest contribution to the value of the line width is made by the collision broadening mechanism. The potassium absorption profile is approximated with high confidence by the Lorentz function with an error in the far wing area of the line.

Author Keywords: mechanisms for broadening the spectral line

articleTitle: Quadrature-modulated signal parameters for fiber-optic lines with semiconductor amplifiers
abstract: A model of a semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) has been developed. Using this model we simulated the distortions of a quadrature-modulated (QAM) signal propagating through a fiber-optic line with SOAs and determined the baudrates and powers which guarantee a non-critical number of errors during transmission.

articleTitle: Spatial-angular scattering of laser radiation by plasma of tungsten, aluminum, sulfur, copper and tantalum
abstract: For the first time, a series of comparative experiments has been conducted to study the scattering of radiation by laser plasma created by the impact of powerful laser radiation on targets made of $\mathrm{W}, \mathrm{Al}, \mathrm{S}, \mathrm{Cu}$, and Ta. The studies were carried out at sub-petawatt values of laser radiation power density in the focusing spot on the target. Scattering diagrams of laser plasma radiation have been obtained in two mutually perpendicular planes.

articleTitle: Transmission Bistability of High-Intensity THz Radiation Propagation in a Nonlinear LiNbO3 Fabry-Perot Interferometer
abstract: This study examines the bistability characteristics of a “mirrorless” Fabry-Perot interferometer utilizing a medium with a highly nonlinear refractive index and low inertia. Through a combination of analytical simulation and experimental investigation, the research reveals that the use of a nonlinear LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> crystal as the medium leads to noticeable optical hysteresis under input intensities of up to $3.5 \times 10^{9} \mathrm{~W} / \mathrm{cm}^{2}$ at a frequency of 0.25 THz.

articleTitle: Effect of administration route on biodistribution of PLGA nanoparticles
abstract: Nanoparticles have gained significant attention as promising drug delivery carriers, offering the potential to revolutionize therapeutic interventions. However, their biodistribution within the body is greatly influenced by the route of administration, impacting their efficacy and safety. Poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid), PLGA, nanoparticles are one of the promising tools for drug delivery due to their high encapsulation efficiency and bioavailability. Here, we report the study of the biodistribution of PLGA nanoparticles loaded with the fluorescent dye Nile Blue upon intravenous and intraperitoneal injections.

articleTitle: Laser formation of biointegrated electronic components based on carbon nanotubes and graphene
abstract: Based on the revealed features of the interaction of laser radiation with carbon nanotubes and graphene, a new approach is proposed for the fabrication of silicon electronic devices and flexible wearable/implantable bioelectronics with controllable electrophysical, optical and mechanical properties. Laser radiation stimulates the formation of covalent graphene-nanotube contacts on a substrate or in a substance. These contacts have led to the development of novel flexible electrodes and electrically conductive constructs for electrogenic tissue recovery and substrates for electrostimulation of cell growth.

articleTitle: Focused ion beam as a tool for prototyping new designs of semiconductor lasers
abstract: We demonstrate the application of direct focused ion beam lithography to realize various designs of optical elements for the modification optical parameters of different types of semiconductor lasers.

articleTitle: Adaptive optical correction of powerful laser beams
abstract: The development of various laser systems and the applications of use of laser beams requires the introduction of such devices that could modify and also improve the wavefront of the laser beams. In these cases, the use of flexible mirrors as well as the whole adaptive optical systems becomes simply very important. In this paper we present our results in the investigation of the efficiency of the use of adaptive optics to compensate for the aberrations of the contemporary laser beam complexes. In this paper we discuss the use of several types of the bimorph deformable mirrors that were successfully installed in laser systems. The results of the measurements of the main characteristics of the developed mirrors such as influence functions of actuators as well as the surface profile of the flexible mirror are presented and discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Generation of random pulsed sequences by switching lateral modes in a quantum-cascade laser
abstract: We study generation of random bit sequences (RBS) with quantum-cascade laser (QCL) and quantum-cascade detector. We show that QCL emission intensity randomly varies due to lateral modes competition and can be converted into RBS.

articleTitle: Optical study of Er3+ and Nd3+/Yb3+-doped CeO2 and CeO2/CeF3 nanoparticles
abstract: In this work, we used a simple dry synthesis of composite nanostructures of $\mathrm{CeO}_{2} / \mathrm{CeF}_{3}$ doped with $\mathbf{E r}^{3+}$ or $\mathbf{N d}^{3+} / \mathbf{Y b}^{3+}$ using ammonium bifluoride $\left(\mathrm{NH}_{4} \mathrm{HF}_{2}\right)$ and annealing in air, respectively. This synthesis procedure makes it possible to obtain double-phase samples with different ratios of $\mathrm{CeO}_{2}\left(\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}\right)$ and $\mathrm{CeF}_{3}\left(\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}\right)$. As for the structure of $\mathrm{CeO}_{2} / \mathrm{CeF}_{3}: \mathbf{E r}^{3+}(\mathbf{0}.1$ at.%), the luminescence intensity of $\mathbf{C e}^{3+}$ and $\mathbf{E r}^{3+}$ ions increases 3.5 times after the fluorination procedure both with UV and resonance pumping, which indicates an increase in the concentration of $\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}$ and $\mathrm{Er}^{3+}$. In the $\mathrm{CeF}_{3}: \mathrm{Nd}^{3+}$ ($0.1 \mathrm{at}. \%$), $\mathbf{Y b}^{3+}$ (0.5 at. $\%$) nanoparticles, under $\mathrm{Nd}^{3+}$ excitation $\mathbf{Y b}^{3+}$ emission is not observed. However, after formation of double-phase $\mathrm{CeO}_{2} /$ CeF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>: $\mathbf{N d}^{3+} / \mathbf{Y b}^{3+}$ samples, both $\mathbf{N d}^{3+}$ and $\mathbf{Y b}^{3+}$ emissions are observed.

articleTitle: Coherent beam combining of a multichannel fiber laser with an automatic alignment system
abstract: In this paper, the implementation of coherent beam combining a seven-channel fiber laser is presented. Channel phase alignment is achieved using a two-stage stochastic parallel gradient algorithm. The influence of the algorithm parameters on the time required for complete phase alignment of the radiation channels is investigated, and optimal values of these parameters are found. The system of automatic channel alignment on one optical axis is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Quantum Correlation in Twin Pulses Generated by Soliton Fission
abstract: We consider soliton fission in a dispersion oscillating fiber. The second-order soliton splits into two identical pulses propagating at different group velocities. Using a back–propagation method we calculate photon-number correlation and squeezing ratio for photon-number fluctuations. With the appropriate modulation period, the correlation function reaches maximum values directly after the split of the soliton and maintains with the further propagation of the pulses. The squeezing ratio increases with the pulse propagation length. Dispersion oscillating fibers offer the possibility of producing entangled sources for quantum communication and computation.

articleTitle: Optical Properties of Modulated Structures in Chiral Liquid Crystals
abstract: Chiral liquid crystals form a number of modulated structures with unusual properties. Here we report experimental studies of the two-dimensional structure forming near the cholesteric-isotropic phase transition. Complex optical patterns with strong nontrivial dependence of the images on light polarization were found and investigated in transmission and reflection.

articleTitle: Noise performance of 89Xnm single-mode VCSELs
abstract: The study of the noise characteristics of the 89X nm single-mode polarization-stable VCSELs based on InGaAs quantum wells is presented. When VCSEL emission is in resonance with the Cs D1 line, the relative intensity noise (RIN) is -105 dB/Hz at 1 Hz and -155 dB/Hz at 100 kHz. The polarization-resolved RIN is slightly higher than RIN but exhibits similar frequency behavior. The frequency noise is ~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>/f Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/Hz in the 1 Hz < f < 100 kHz range, which corresponds to the emission linewidth of ~30 MHz.

Index Terms: Singlemode Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Lasers

articleTitle: Terahertz field and carrier dynamics in optically excited layer at the surface of a GaAs crystal
abstract: Results of FDTD modeling of the terahertz field and carrier transient dynamics in an optically excited layer at the surface of a GaAs crystal are presented. The field demonstrates a monotonic or oscillatory decay on a subpicosecond time-scale, depending on the parameters.

articleTitle: Spectral-kinetic characteristics and sensitized luminescence of LiYxLu1-xF4 mixed crystals with Tm3+ and Ho3+ ions
abstract: We report about spectral and luminescence decay characteristics of the concentration series of $\mathrm{LiY}_{\mathbf{x}} \mathrm{Lu}_{1-x} \mathrm{~F}_{4}$ mixed crystals doped with $\mathbf{T m}^{3+}$ and $\mathrm{Ho}^{3+}$ ions. The sensitized luminescence and polarization dependent spectral characteristics of investigated crystals where some broadening of spectral lines is evidenced are presented and discussed. Measured data allowed us to estimate the Förster radius and energy transfer rates for the system of $\mathrm{Tm}^{3+}-\mathrm{Ho}^{3+}$ ions in $\mathrm{LiY}_{\mathbf{x}} \mathrm{Lu}_{1-\mathrm{x}} \mathrm{F}_{4}$ mixed crystals.

articleTitle: Interaction of the quantum electromagnetic field with solid-state nanostructures under nonlinearity
abstract: Dynamics of excitation induced in solid-state planar nanosystems by non-classical electromagnetic fields is investigated under the Kerr self-phase nonlinearity. New peculiarities of the quantum state evolution are found due to mutual interplay between the electron-photon coupling and the self-phase modulation. The possibility to control the excitation by changing the frequency detuning of the field and non-linearity degree is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Fluorescently controlled investigation of super-enhancers with CRISPR interference and CRISPR prime editing systems
abstract: In the evolving landscape of genomic research, our study delves into the intricate exploration of super-enhancers, pivotal and controversial elements exerting profound influence over gene expression. Utilizing CRISPR interference and CRISPR prime editing systems, our work yields promising results and opens avenues for future research to refine and expand these approaches across diverse cell types.

articleTitle: Stimulated emission in a complex background
abstract: Our study focuses on examining the induced emission of an atom triggered by a wave packet photon. We aim to understand the relationship between the quantum numbers and characteristics of the initial reference photon and the final two-photon state. This investigation holds promise for advancing photon detection techniques. We begin by considering the emission stimulated by a plane wave reference photon as the first step.

articleTitle: Gigawatt few-cycle mid-IR pulses generated from advanced non-oxide nonlinear crystals
abstract: Advanced nonlinear materials - LiGaS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (LGS), $\mathrm{HgGa}_{2} \mathrm{~S}_{4}$ (HGS) and BaGa<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> GeS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> (BGGS) - were studied for parametric down conversion of Cr:Forsterite laser pulses into 1.5 $-8 \mu \mathrm{m}$ spectral region. Total conversion efficiency as high as $18 \%$ was achieved in HGS based OPA resulting in 0.4 - 2.4-gigawatt 80 fs pulses. Using LGS, broadband mid-IR pulses with energy up to $20 \mu \mathrm{J}$ were obtained. After bulk compression in a Ge plate, a pulse duration as low as 60 fs was measured, corresponding to three optical cycles of $5.9 \mu \mathrm{m}$ carrier wavelength. New non-oxide BGGS crystal was compared with HGS, showing great potential for efficient parametric amplification in mid-IR. The developed source provides numerous opportunities for time-resolved pump-probe experiments and opens access to attosecond physics and material sciences.

articleTitle: Biocompatible composite material for the regeneration of large tissue defects
abstract: This paper presents a technology for formation of biocompatible material for bone defect regeneration based on carbon nanotubes and biopolymers. Studies of the structure of the formed samples indicate the presence of the necessary characteristics. Biocompatibility studies have shown the applicability of the developed material for the regeneration of large tissue defects.

articleTitle: 1030 nm amplified spontaneous emission suppression in Yb-doped fiber amplifier operating near 976 nm
abstract: A newly-designed Yb-doped fiber type, intended to enhance 976 nm lasing by suppressing the spectral component including 1030 nm amplified spontaneous emission (ASE), was thoroughly researched. To implement an extremely sharp short-bandpass spectral filter, several suitably selected high-index absorber rods were incorporated into the fiber cladding. Thus, the concept of such a filter allows for a relatively accurate stop-band position adjustment as a result of the highly fiber-bend-dependent state of the intermodes resonance core-rod interaction. Finally, the impact of enhancing the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of the fiber amplifier emitting at a wavelength of 976 nm, by shifting the stop-band, is justified and demonstrated in this study.
