articleTitle: Spectral properties of crystalline aluminum phthalocyanine nanoparticles and the possibility of their use in biophotonics
abstract: The enhancement of phototheranostics specificity and selectivity represents a pressing objective. The selectivity of the procedure can be significantly increased by using AIPc nanoparticles as photosensitizers. The present study investigates the occurrence of optical effects manifested by the interaction of crystalline AIPc nanoparticles with the microenvironment and laser irradiation by means of time-resolved laser spectroscopy, analysis of multispectral fluorescence microimages, microstructure and X-ray diffraction techniques.

articleTitle: Spectroscopic intraoperative diagnostics of tumors during photodynamic therapy
abstract: developed methods of spectroscopic diagnostics make it possible to move on to personalized photodynamic therapy (PDT) and represent methods of intraoperative PDT dosimetry. The effective energy dose during PDT of a tumor can be determined by a combined assessment of the intensity of photosensitizer (PS) photobleaching and the level of oxygenation.

articleTitle: Generation of long-lived strong magnetic fields in laser targets with cylindrical micro-channels
abstract: We consider generation of large magnetic fields based on electron inertia in cylindrical shells and microchannel target irradiated by circular polarized intense ultrashort laser pulses. The optimal (for large and long life magnetic field) laser and target parameters were found by using the analytical model and 3D PIC simulations. It is shown that such fields slow down the structure expansion, which can be used to obtain ultrahigh energy densities in focal volume laser plasma.

articleTitle: Contrast, angular and spectral selectivity of a temperature-noncritical Pockels cell on KTP crystal
abstract: The results of experimental investigations of contrast, angular and spectral properties for Pockels cell based on single temperature-noncritical KTP crystal are presented.

articleTitle: PCM for driving active THz modulators: frequency and polarization sensitivity
abstract: Optical properties of phase-change materials (PCM) GeTe and GeTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> were studied. Active planar metamaterials based on PCM with ultrafast switching of THz field characteristics were developed. A new technique for obtaining the complex refractive index of metamaterials based on simultaneous measurement of reflection and transmission of THz radiation was proposed and experimentally confirmed. Such anisotropic effects as optical activity and circular dichroism in the interaction of THz field with active metamaterials were investigated.

articleTitle: Identification of up-conversion luminescence lines of fluorophosphate glass doped with ytterbium and thulium ions by respective nonlinearity of the upconversion process
abstract: The up-conversion luminescence (UCL) spectra of fluorophosphate glasses doped with a pair of rare earth ions (REI) of ytterbium and thulium in different combinations of their concentrations were studied under continuous excitation at a wavelength of 975 nm. Each of the observed USL bands resulted from the sum of several luminescence processes corresponding to radiation from different excited states of thulium ions. These processes are characterized by different degrees of nonlinearity in the number of required absorbed photons necessary to excite these states. We analyze the influence of pump power and doping ion concentration on the contributions to the UCL spectra caused by excitation processes with various nonlinearities. We found that the appearance of several lines in each of the four spectral regions of ultrasonic luminescence is typical for low concentrations of thulium ions (from a tenth to a thousandth of a percent) and relatively high concentrations of ytterbium ions (from 4 to 10 percent). When the thulium ion concentration was increased to 3 percent with ytterbium ion concentration of 5 percent, the UCL was observed predominantly in the range 755– 840 nm with a maximum near 793 nm.

articleTitle: Generation of Tunable Ultraviolet Pulses Using Gas Ionization By Chirped Two-Color Pulses
abstract: We propose a method for generating pulses of ultraviolet radiation with stable phase and tunable frequency. The method is based on gas ionization by two-color laser pulses with frequency chirp of opposite sign and variable time delay. Changing the time delay allows simple tuning of the generation frequency near the fourth harmonic of the fundamental field.

articleTitle: Reflectivity Changes In GST225 Thin Film Induced By Laser Pulses With Variable Duration
abstract: Phase transitions of GST225 thin films with a thickness of 150 nm were induced by laser pulses with durations ranging from 20 to 140 ns and energies ranging from 1 to 15 μJ. The transitions lasted from 0.4 to 0.6 μs, and the optical contrast reached up to 90%. The study also demonstrated the possibility of two-level transitions.

articleTitle: Rigidochromic porphyrazine dyes: smart molecules for sensing and cancer treatment
abstract: Tetracyanotetra(aryl)porphyrazines are a unique group of dyes combining properties of molecular rotors and photodynamic agents. The fluorescence lifetime and quantum yield of these compounds are highly dependent on local viscosity, so they can be used as sensors of intracellular viscosity. The rigidochromic behaviours of the compounds provides a tool to quantify cell damage in real time during photodynamic cancer treatment.

articleTitle: Deactivating coatings of the discharge channel walls and average radiation power of a nitrogen laser
abstract: Theinfluence of heterogeneous dispersion of the lower metastable states of molecular nitrogen on the parameters of a low-pressure N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-laser has been studied. Graphite, boric acid, hopcalite ($40 \% \mathrm{CuO}+60 \% \mathrm{MnO}_{2}$), titanium oxide and chromium oxide were used as decontamination materials. The most effective are graphite, boric acid and chromium oxide. The use of these materials provides an increase in frequency by 1.4-1.5 times while maintaining the radiation energy per pulse at the level of 80-105 $\mu \mathrm{J}$.

articleTitle: Few-fs half-cycle pulse train with an ultra-high pulse repetition rate from nested quantum wells
abstract: We propose a simple and compact structure, consisting of a pair of nested quantum wells, as a source of a train of half-cycle pulses of few-fs duration when driven by an external electric field. We theoretically analyze the spatio-temporal dynamics of such a structure and demonstrate the possibility of the generation of ultrafast half-cycle pulse trains with ultra-high pulse repetition rates of tens of THz.

articleTitle: Study of the temperature stability of the parameters of a fiber-optic resonator with preservation of polarization
abstract: The temperature dependences of FSR, FWHM, Finesse, Q-factor and the output power of a fiber-optic resonator assembled on an optical polarization maintaining Panda-type fiber in the temperature range of $-30 \ldots+50^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ were obtained. The studied resonator demonstrated stability of parameters within $10 \%$ for a given temperature range. Such resonator can be useful as a sensitive element of resonator fiber-optic gyroscopes.

articleTitle: New method of controlling the axis of laser radiation in Anderson differential cuvette in mobile refractometer
abstract: The necessity of measuring the refractive index of a liquid medium in the range of 1.230 to 2.830 with an accuracy of 0.0001 for unambiguous express control of its condition has been justified. A design of a mobile refractometer with Anderson’s differential cuvette and a new methodology for controlling the axis of laser emission has been developed to ensure measurement of the refractive index with this accuracy throughout the specified range.

articleTitle: Nd:YAG laser terminal level relaxation time direct evaluation and its considering at picosecond pulse amplification
abstract: Direct measurements of the terminal level relaxation time of Nd:YAG laser transition with 1064 nm wavelength were fulfilled based on the gain recovery diagnostics after picosecond saturating pulse passage through the amplifying medium. Experimental results clearly demonstrate that the relaxation time of the terminal level does not exceed 70 ps. The obtained result seems important in view of developing effective longitudinally diode-pumped amplifiers operating near the saturation conditions with a short interval between successive passes through the gain medium.

articleTitle: Using neural networks to reconstruct the wavefront of laser radiation based on the focal distribution of fluence near the waist
abstract: The paper proposed a method for determining wavefront distortions from the intensity distribution in two planes of laser pulse waist: in focus and out of focus. For the wavefront reconstruction task, we propose to use deep convolutional neural networks. To train the models, we used numerically generated data using Zernike modes. The method has shown good efficiency and can significantly speed up and improve the quality of calibration of an adaptive optical system.

articleTitle: Upconversion Nanoparticles for Diagnosis and Targeted Treatment of Cancer
abstract: Significant progress in the field of nanobiotechnology has contributed to the improvement of tools and methods for diagnosis and treatment of such socially significant diseases as cancer. The creation of multifunctional complexes is one of the effective tools of modern biomedicine. We created theranostic complexes based on upconversion luminescent nanoparticles and the recombinant targeted toxin DARPin-LoPE. We have demonstrated the high toxicity of the developed complexes against target tumor cells. In addition, we documented the selective accumulation of the resulting theranostic complexes in tumors characterized by overexpression of the HER2 receptor. In general, the complexes have high potential as effective tools for theranostics of oncological diseases.

articleTitle: LIPSS on titanium plate prepared by nanosecond pulses
abstract: The method of nanosecond laser periodic structuring of the titanium surface is presented for the aim of further studying optical and mechanical properties of the formed structures, such as reflection and refraction in the visible and infrared wavelength ranges, as well as the wettability of structured titanium.

articleTitle: 6-wavelength VIS-SWIR laser with acousto-optic attenuation
abstract: We propose a technique for simultaneous selection and attenuation of up to eight spectral components through smooth tuning the frequencies and amplitudes of acoustic waves in acousto-optic crystal equipped with two piezoelectric transducers. We installed this acousto-optic tunable filter in a multi-wavelength system based on a pulsed Nd:YAG laser (1064 nm) with intracavity parametric generation of signal wave radiation (1572 nm) and extracavity conversion of light into higher harmonics and total frequencies. Experiments demonstrate repeatable 0-100% attenuation of 6 spectral components (452 nm, 532 nm, 635 nm, 786 nm, 1064 nm and 1572 nm). This laser system may have multiple applications in interferometry, color reproduction, multi-spectral imaging and other fields.

Author Keywords: visible and short wave infrared range

articleTitle: Enhanced stability of SHG in PPLN incorporated in the Pierce oscillator circuit
abstract: We introduce a novel approach to temperature stabilization of nonlinear-optical (n-o) crystals without using external temperature sensors. The crystal itself is turned into temperature sensor by measuring its piezoelectric resonance frequency which is related to the average temperature. With the proposed method we were able to achieve stable second harmonic generation (SHG) in periodically poled lithium niobate crystal (PPLN) at $30 \%$ more power compared to the case of application of external temperature sensors. Long-term stability of SH power was also enhanced.

articleTitle: Object detection by a microjoule-pulse LiDAR through a through a 18-m water layer: docking & navigation
abstract: The backscattering signal of a LiDAR pulse (3 ns, 532 nm, 2 μJ/pulse) was recorded for the first time through 18 m of water and 7 m of air. Reflectors placed on the target surface are found to multiply the backscattering signal. Underwater maneuvering of unmanned robots, docking and navigation in flooded areas using a LiDAR with eye-safe radiation level (≤1 μJ/cm2) is discussed.

Author Keywords: remote sensing in strongly scattering media

articleTitle: Endovenous laser coagulation of large diameter varicose veins.
abstract: Thepurpose of this report is to justify the selection of the optimal method of endovenous laser coagulation (EVLC) of varicose veins of large (more than 2 cm) diameter.

articleTitle: New scheme of Faraday isolator with dV/dT distortions compensation
abstract: The Faraday isolator is typically used to prevent unwanted back-propagation of radiation in complex laser systems. At high-average-power laser radiation, the isolation degree of such devices is limited by thermally induced depolarization. The main sources of radiation depolarization in the Faraday isolator are thermally-induced linear birefringence and the temperature dependence of the Verdet constant. Usually, the contribution of the first significantly exceeds the contribution of the second. However, in a number of practically important cases, the opposite situation is observed (cryogenic temperatures, magneto-optical elements in critical orientation [C]). Today, there are no satisfying solutions to this problem. In this work, a new scheme of Faraday isolators with dV/dT distortion compensation was proposed. The comparison of isolation between the proposed scheme and what are known from the literature is observed.

articleTitle: Physical factors causing zero drift and noise in a solid-state laser gyroscope based on YAG: Cr4+ at mode locking
abstract: This paper presents the results of creating a solid-state YAG: $\mathrm{Cr}^{4+}$ laser gyroscope working in mode locking. Perimeter control system uses an absorbing cell with acetylene. An electro-optical modulator is used to create a frequency dither; it creates a phase shift at the moment the pulse passes. The main factors influencing the gyroscope zero drift and noise are determined.

articleTitle: Microring optimization for the tunable vortex beam emitter
abstract: Light beams bearing orbital angular momentum (OAM) are perspectives in different applications, including communication and sensing systems, chemistry, and microbiology. One can apply the topological charge control to improve information security or to provide an additional orthogonal basis to speed the data exchange up. Detecting OAM changes may help measure the solid rotation parameters or atmospheric turbulence. Our work presents a novel method for optimizing the micro-ring resonator (MRR) as a vortex beam emitter with tunable OAM order. We added the periodic structure to the ring waveguide to transform the whispering gallery modes into radiation modes. Depositing phase change material Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> on the ring waveguide provided us with an instrument to control the OAM order. This material changes its refractive index when switching from an amorphous phase (for this case, the refractive index equals 3.285) to crystalline (here, the refractive index reaches 4.050). All values are given the wavelength 1550 nm. This material also has another advantage: the zero imaginary part of the refractive index provides low optical loss. We optimized the MRR to provide the radiated energy’s maximum flux density and to keep the radiated power constant on the OAM switching, which helps us avoid the parasitic amplitude modulation of an optical beam. We also show some analytical approaches to simplify the simulation complexity. One can easily apply the proposed approach to optimize optical beam emitters carrying OAM for various applications.

articleTitle: Study of the spectral and kinetic characteristics of the Er3+ ion in BaY1.8Lu0.2F8 mixed crystals to assess the possibility of continuous laser oscillation at a wavelength of 2.7 μm
abstract: Herewe present the spectral and kinetic characteristics of $\mathrm{Er}^{3+}$ ions in the heavily doped $\mathrm{BaY}_{1.8} \mathrm{Lu}_{0.2} \mathrm{~F}_{8}$ mixed crystals and evaluate the possibility of continuous laser oscillation at a wavelength of $2.7 \mu \mathrm{m}$.

articleTitle: Are picosecond laser pulses applicable for microsurgery of zona pellucida of mammalian embryo?
abstract: Infrared picosecond laser pulses are used for microsurgery of mouse embryos at late stages of preimplantation development. The width of the cut made by a series of laser pulses at the zona pellucida of the mouse embryo is studied for different laser beam velocities and pulse energies.

articleTitle: Surgery guidance in orthopedics and dentistry
abstract: An urgent problem in biophotonics is the search and development of new methods for objective assessment of tissue parameters during surgical operations. This study examines two problems related to orthopedics and dentistry: assessing the condition of the tissues of the knee joint during arthroscopy, as well as assessing the distance to the dental pulp when removing infected dentin due to caries. An approach to solving these problems was studied using an optic fiber implementation of the diffuse reflectance spectroscopy method when measuring explants obtained during surgical interventions, as well as when measuring directly during operations. To optimize the measuring configuration, Monte Carlo simulation of light propagation in tissues was used; based on the experimental data obtained, methods for determining tissue parameters using machine learning methods were constructed. Further options for the improvement of these techniques are discussed.

articleTitle: Quantum dots. Hydrophilization techniques for analytical applications
abstract: Quantum dots are semiconductor crystals with unique optical properties. Analytical applications are made possible due to the stability of the crystal, the ability to vary the fluorescence wavelength, and the capacity for non-radiative energy transfer. They are influenced by the composition, structure and coating of QDs.

articleTitle: Simulation of infrared radiation backscattering in multylayer tissue models
abstract: Calculating and studying the characteristics of infrared radiation scattered by multilayer systems expands the possibilities of noninvasive diagnostics of the state of biological tissues. We present Monte Carlo simulation results of backscattering from a four-layer bio-tissue model based on the solution of the Bethe-Salpeter equation, focusing on the skin-skullcerebrospinal fluid-brain system. The calculations reveal that the angular and spatial dependences of the backscatter intensity are extremely sensitive to the penetration of blood into the cerebrospinal fluid layer, suggesting potential applications in the rapid diagnosis of head injuries.

articleTitle: Polarization coupling in a bent otical waveguide based on thin film lithium niobate
abstract: Inthe present paper the simulation of modes in waveguides based on thin film lithium niobate was performed. Further, the coupling coefficients depending on the waveguide rotation angle were obtained. The results showed the maximal absolute value of the coupling coefficient was around 0.013.

articleTitle: Multi-Frequency Laser Spectroscopy of Sub-Doppler Resonances in Miniature Cs Vapour Cells
abstract: A new method of atomic sub-Doppler spectroscopy was developed. The key feature is that the new method uses dual-frequency laser beams in two different optical scheme: with linearly polarized counterpropagating beams with a mutual angle between the polarizations equal to 90 and 45 degrees,, respectively. Due to the CPT effect, a resonance of the opposite sign relative to the saturated absorption resonances was observed.

articleTitle: Modulation Instability Threshold Increase in Phase-sensitive Optical Time-domain Reflectometer by Narrowband Optical Filtration
abstract: We demonstrate the threshold increase of Modulation Instability in phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometer by implementing 10 GHz-bandwidth optical filter.

articleTitle: Second harmonic generation with two noncollinear passage walk-off compensation
abstract: The results of experimental investigations for the walk-off compensation second harmonic generation with noncollinear propagation on direct and reverse passage in a single crystal are presented.

articleTitle: Nonlinear components of energy, momentum and angular momentum of Gaussian beams in self-focusing in isotropic gyrotropic media
abstract: The magnitudes of contributions of the related to local and nonlocal parts of nonlinear optical response of the medium terms of the expressions for the electromagnetic energy density, momentum density, angular momentum density and the corresponding flux densities in self-focusing of elliptically polarized light beam in nonabsorbing isotropic gyrotropic medium is determined.

articleTitle: Development of multicolor parametric amplifier based on sub-ps ytterbium laser
abstract: Based on nonlinear interactions, a universal multicolor converter of sub-ps pulses of ytterbium lasers in a few cycle femtosecond pulses with a tunable central wavelength in the range from 650 to 2500 nm has been created. The possibility of parametric amplification of these pulses to the mJ energy level by various approaches has been investigated. The results obtained are used in the upgrade of the laser complex PEARL.

articleTitle: Dual-pumped Integrated Microring Degenerate Optical Parametric Oscillator
abstract: We study the nonlinear degenerate four-wave mixing in high-Q integrated Si3N4 ring microresonator dualpumped by continuous wave lasers. Highly efficient degenerate optical parametric oscillator is observed experimentally.

articleTitle: Optical compressor as a spatial filter of PW laser beams before nonlinear temporal compression stage
abstract: It is demonstrated that optical compressor operates as a filter of spatial harmonics of powerful laser beams. There are two factors of filtering in time and in space. The facts lead to suppressing small-scale self-focusing development inside a nonlinear sample used for spectrum broadening in additional temporal compression stage based on CafCA method.

articleTitle: Photoluminescence enhancement of nanowires in IR-range induced by surface plasmon
abstract: Nanowires are promising solids for creating efficient optoelectronic and nanophotonic devices. Here, we study the optical properties of single InP/InAsP/InP nanowire transferred to Ag/SiOx plasmonic substrate. For the first time, photoluminescence enhancement for these nanowires due to exciton-plasmon interaction was demonstrated.

articleTitle: Growth and physical properties of MgWO4 crystal
abstract: MgWO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> single crystals were grown by top seed solution growth method. Their thermal conductivity, mechanical strength properties, as well as dispersion and thermal coefficients of the refraction indices were measured.

articleTitle: Two-temperature distribution in task of laser cooling in fields with a polarisation gradient of atoms
abstract: We suggested a two-temperature model of velocity distribution for laser cooling of neutral atoms with not small enough recoil parameter. Analysis of temperatures of “cold” and “hot” fraction and their proportions showed better description of ensemble energy. It is of significant importance for solving the problem of achieving deeper laser cooling and analysis of cooled atomic clouds.

articleTitle: Discovery of novel fluorophores in the human organism with quantitative structure-property relationship approach
abstract: Endogenous fluorophores are of high interest for application in biomedical diagnostics. Y et, the list of known and commonly used fluorophores is limited. Here we demonstrate the possibility of identification new fluorophores using “bottom-up” approach with help of machine learning approaches to predict optical properties for organic molecules by its chemical structure. We show the presented approach have high accuracy in restoring optical properties for commonly known endogeneous fluorophores and then use it to identify new fluorescent sources using multiple large open-source databases of molecules presented in human body, while also comparing the results obtained experimentally on the new fluorophore identified in thyroid and parathyroid glands and other tissues.

articleTitle: Self-Action of Structured Light Beams in Amorphous Azobenzene-Containing Polymer
abstract: The action of the light beams of various structure and their transformation in a thin layer of the polymethacrylate azobenzene-containing polymer is studied. This material shows high optical nonlinearity related to trans-cis transitions of absorbing fragments, whose reorientation can induce optical anisotropy and affect refractive indices. Additional methyl groups provide higher sensitivity in the visible range $\left(n_{2} \sim 10^{-3} \mathbf{c m}^{2} / W\right.$ for $532 \mathbf{n m}$), not affecting high IR transparency, which is promising for telecommunication applications. It is shown that, depending on the polarization and structure of the beam, it is possible to induce negative or positive anisotropy in an initially amorphous sample, as well as to create a complex spatial distribution of optical axes, similar to that of vortex converters. The polymer under study possesses highly local nonlinear response, which linearly depends on delivered energy over a wide range of exposure time and beam power. The TEM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode aberrational self-action combined with polarization optical microscopy was used to determine the value, sign and profile of anisotropy.

articleTitle: Athermal design of Yb:YAG thick disk active element
abstract: We propose a method for suppression of thermally-induced wavefront distortions in disk laser active element. The method utilizes a specially-shaped heat conducting plate which provides efficient heat removal from the active element only in its pumped region. The absence of thermal contact beyond active region blocks the radial heat flow and reduces thermally-induced lensing. The method was implemented with thick-disk Yb:YAG active element and composite $\mathrm{Yb}: \mathrm{YAG} /$ sapphire. Zero thermal lens active element was demonstrated in the experiment.

articleTitle: Targeted magnetic nanoparticles for cancer diagnosis and treatment
abstract: Cancer poses a significant healthcare challenge worldwide, spurring the investigation of innovative treatment methods. Over the past few years, nanomaterials have garnered considerable attention, in particular, targeted nanoformulations due to their high specificity of delivery to molecular targets and reduced systemic toxicity for the organism. Here we report the study of the cellular delivery of targeted fluorescent magnetic nanoparticles to human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), clinically significant oncomarker, on the surface of cancer cells.

articleTitle: Zernike-based hill-climbing algorithm for super-Gaussian and doughnut-like laser beam shaping by means of a phase-only spatial light modulator
abstract: Adaptive optical system with phase-only special light modulator and intensity analyzer for laser beam shaping was assembled. The newly developed Zernike-based hill-climbing algorithm for creating the super-Gaussian and doughnut-like intensity distributions was developed. It was shown that about 60 % and 75 % of the initial beam energy was concentrated in the focal spot for the doughnut-like and flat-top intensity distributions, correspondingly.

articleTitle: Dual-laser self-injection locking microcomb regime switching
abstract: The research demonstrates the generation of soliton microcombs and perfect soliton crystals using a bichromatical pump by self-injection-locked laser diodes. We unveil intense cross-talk between laser diodes through the microring, providing the possibility of deterministic switching of generated soliton states by manipulating the detuning of one of the lasers.

articleTitle: Delay measurement in fiber optic devices using a tunable delay line
abstract: The diagram and principle of operation of an installation for measuring signal propagation delays in fiber-optic devices, built on the basis of a reference tunable optical delay line, are presented

articleTitle: Analysis of the gradient method for laser calorimetry and analytical correction factors
abstract: We have obtained the analytical expression for the derivative difference value used in the gradient method the lase1r calorimetry (LC). It was reinterpreted in terms of average temperature regarding the piezolectric resonance laser calorimetry (PRLC), which to the best of our knowledge has been done for the first time. Correction factors in the cases of $L C$ and PRLC were also estimated. We propose to choose the position of the temperature sensor in the LC based on the minimal value of correction factors.

articleTitle: Biocompatible pH sensors based on the Re(I) luminophores containing oligo(ethylene glycol) groups
abstract: A novel family of biocompatible Re(I) complexes containing oligo(ethylene glycol) groups with sensory response onto pH variations in physiologically relevant interval were successfully synthesized. Preliminary in vitro experiments showed low cytotoxicity and easy internalization of the obtained complexes in cell culture.

articleTitle: Dispersion of effective nonlinearity for frequency conversion in biaxial crystals
abstract: The results of dispersion estimation for effective nonlinearity in biaxial crystals for different point groups are presented. Phenomenon of nonlinearity dispersion is caused by pronounced changing of the angle to the optical axis of the crystal, which is typical for many recently synthesized media.

articleTitle: Coherent combination of 4 laser channels amplified in a single Yb:YAG crystal
abstract: The scheme for amplification of 4 beams in single-rod Yb:YAG amplifier and their coherent combining using a tiled aperture scheme is proposed and demonstrated experimentally. This approach will allow scaling average and peak power.

articleTitle: Metabolic stress of tumor microenvironment during photothermal therapy: activation of an immune antitumor response
abstract: The work presents a study of intracellular temperature and metabolic stress during photothermal therapy, affecting the triggered cell death processes of different types. The obtained data will make it possible to optimize the laser exposure parameters for photothermal therapy, increasing the thermosensitivity of cancer and immune cells triggering the process of immunogenic cell death.

articleTitle: Study of the possibility of using dielectric nanoparticles doped with rare earth ions for the treatment of tumors under non-contact exposure to near-IR laser radiation
abstract: We investigated the possibilities of using ZrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-30 mol.% Yb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> particles in combination with 980 nm laser irradiation for the treatment of subcutaneous tumors. Cytotoxicity of these particles was studied and in-vivo experiments (on mice) were conducted.

articleTitle: Electron beam Pumped Ultraviolet Light Source (240-267nm) based on GaN/AlN MQW Structures with Output Pulsed Power of Several Tens Watts
abstract: Using electrons with energy about 15 keV, electron source based on a ferroelectric cathode and GaN/AIN MQW Structures the following values of power of UV-pulse radiation were obtained: $50 \mathrm{~W}(\lambda=240 \mathrm{~nm}, J=2240 \mathrm{~mA}), 69 \mathrm{~W}$ $(\lambda=248 \mathrm{~nm}, J=2500 \mathrm{~mA}), 71 W(\lambda=267 \mathrm{~nm}, J=2340 \mathrm{~mA})$

articleTitle: Generation of Second and Third Harmonics of XUV Pulse by Noble-Gas Atoms in the Presence of Intense Infrared Field
abstract: We study numerically the generation of the second and third harmonics of an extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) pulse by noble-gas atoms subjected to an intense infrared pulse. Our numerical calculations are based on the solution of time-dependent Kohn-Sham equations for argon, krypton, and xenon atoms. We show that all electrons in the outer shell of an atom contribute significantly to the generation of XUV-pulse harmonics. Electrons from internal orbitals may also contribute significantly at high XUV frequencies due to the resonance transitions from the internal states. It is shown that the generation of XUV harmonics can be used to measure the nonlinear susceptibilities in the XUV range and monitor the phase of the XUV pulse.

articleTitle: Statistical characteristics of optical vortices in a beam with an initial phase set by Zernike polynomials and by a turbulent screen
abstract: With the use of numerical experiment methods we compare distributions of optical vortices in beams whose initial phase was formed by Zernike polynomials and beams with the phase set by a screen simulating atmospheric turbulence. As was shown the statistical characteristics of the singular points in both cases (polynomials and screen) satisfied the requirements of the Central limit theorem. At the same time, differences were observed in the dependence of the number of vortices on the length of the propagation path.

articleTitle: Experimental observation of Weibel instability in the astrophysicaly and Fast Ignition relevant plasmas induced by ultrashort 250 TW laser pulse
abstract: Weibel instability was observed experimentally in plasma generated after irradiation a solid target with a 250 TW ultrashort laser pulse at the PEARL petawatt laser facility. The influence of laser radiation intensity and an external magnetic field on generation of the Weibel instability has been investigated.

articleTitle: Active Region Overheating in Quantum Cascade Lasers
abstract: We study the QCL active region overheating and discuss the effects of nonequilibrium heat dissipation on laser performance. We show that the effective thermal management fundamentally depends on the active region material properties.

articleTitle: Calculation of a frequency of laser beam parameter changes in a turbulent medium
abstract: Results of a laboratory and numerical experiments are analysed and compared in the paper. In experiments a laser radiation propagated in a randomly inhomogeneous medium. The main objective of the analysis was calculation of the frequency of the beam parameter changes. The study was conducted to determine the speed of the adaptive system operation required to compensate for distortions.

articleTitle: Compact TEA-CO2 laser with pulse repetition rate up to 2.5 kHz
abstract: The influence of the parameters of high-voltage pump pulses on the formation of stable volume discharges in the gap $\mathrm{V}=24 \times 1.8 \times 0.8=34 \mathrm{~cm}^{3}$ in CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-laser mixtures with a high content of carbon dioxide at pulse repetition frequencies up to 2.5 kHz has been studied. Laser pulses with an energy per pulse of 80-120 mJ with a minimum duration of 25-35 nanoseconds were obtained.

Author Keywords: energy and duration of radiation pulses

articleTitle: Frequency domain model for high power solid-state laser amplifiers
abstract: The numerical model of the laser amplification process based on the nonlinear Schrödinger equation for systems with simultaneously high peak power and pulse repetition rate has been developed. A model describes the interaction of the amplified radiation and the active element in the frequency domain without loss of phase relationships between the corresponding spectral components. The model is verified by comparing experimental and simulated results.

articleTitle: High-Order Harmonics Generation by Solid Slabs in Two-Color Infrared and Ultraviolet Field
abstract: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) by a solid slab in an infrared (IR) field with the addition of an ultraviolet (UV) pulse is studied numerically based on the developed computer code for solving the one-dimensional time-dependent Kohn–Sham equations for linear chain of ions. It is shown that the addition of a weak UV pulse with photon energy greater than the band gap leads to a strong change in the HHG spectrum. The dependence of the harmonic yield near the HHG cutoff on the time delay between the IR and UV pulses represents an interference pattern with oscillation frequency equal to UV-pulse frequency and an averaged shape coinciding with the envelope of the UV pulse.

articleTitle: Design and interactions of luminescent nanoparticles in analytical systems
abstract: Luminescent nanoparticles and nanoclusters represent a promising tool for imaging and bioanalysis. The sophisticated design of nanoparticles allows them to be used as active and passive tags to detect the presence of various components. The potential of nanoparticles to alter the optical signal in response to the presence of analytes and their analytical applications are discussed. The influence of biomatrix components on luminescent signals is also considered.

articleTitle: Implementation of reinforcement learning algorithms for fiber mode-locked lasers
abstract: We demonstrate the use of various types of reinforcement learning algorithms for the following tasks: self-starting, stability under temperature fluctuations, and optimization of the pulsed regimes of fiber mode-locked lasers. The feasibility of implementing reinforcement algorithms in a multi-stable system such as fiber-locked lasers is demonstrated. The main problems with reinforcement learning algorithms are discussed.

articleTitle: Thulium fiber laser: Experimental study on biological tissue
abstract: One of the important issues, to develop an optimal mode for minimally invasive outpatient turbinoplasty surgery. In this paper, we select the optimal mode at a wavelength of 1.94 μm on calf kidney tissue to achieve maximum coagulation without ablation of the superficial and interstitial layer. The optimal mode of exposure was concluded.

articleTitle: Resonant Scattering under Two-Photon Excitation in a GaN Crystal
abstract: The resonant hyper-Raman scattering process in a wurtzite GaN crystal was theoretically studied, taking into account the possible dipole transitions to the deeper valence band.

articleTitle: Pulse mode of optical exitating the MDMO-PPV polymer embadded in a porous silicon microcavity for detecting nitroaromatic compounds
abstract: abstract-Fluorescent detection of nitroaromatic molecules is a rapidly advancing field with significant implications for environmental monitoring, security, and biomedical research. The main issue in creating fluorescent sensors for molecules of nitroaromatic compounds is the inevitable decrease of fluorescence even in the absence of interaction of the analyte with the target molecules. This paper presents the results of a study of the time dependences of the fluorescence amplitude of the MDMO-PPV polymer under different optical excitation modes. Due to the results of the work, conclusions were drawn about the excitation parameters at which a further reduction of the average radiation intensity does not affect noticeably on the stability of the fluorescence of the polymer.

articleTitle: Broadband thin-film lithium niobate waveguide modulator with high-order mode suppression
abstract: A high-frequency phase modulator based on a multimode optical waveguide made of thin-film lithium niobate was designed and studied. The modulator was fabricated in a topology with metal electrodes placed near the edges of the waveguide to suppress higher-order waveguide modes and provide quasi-single-mode light propagation. Efficient modulation with a voltage-length product $V_{\pi} L \approx 4 \mathrm{~V} \cdot \mathrm{cm}$ and a bandwidth of more than 30 GHz have been successfully demonstrated.

articleTitle: Photosensitization of singlet molecular oxygen by bacterial C40 carotenoids
abstract: Time-resolved measurement of photosensitized luminescence of singlet oxygen (SO) has been applied to studies of SO generation and quenching by C40 carotenoids (phytofluene, zeta-carotene, neurosporene, lycopene, rhodopin and spirilloxanthin) having (5-13) conjugated double bonds (CDB) in their molecules. It has been found for the first time that the studied carotenoids which were always considered as strong quenchers of SO, combine this property with an ability of SO generation upon photoexcitation.

articleTitle: Temporal Transformation of Noise-Like Pulse Bunches in an Er-doped Fiber Laser
abstract: A fiber laser generating noise-like two-pulse bunches with duration of $\sim 66 \ \mathrm{fs}$ is presented. The transformation of these pulses into a multi-bound soliton regime with a duration of 142 fs is investigated.

articleTitle: Dynamics of long period pulsations when intra-cavity loss change
abstract: Wereport on the dynamics of laser generation during the transition from stable mode-locking to mode-locking accompanied by long period pulsations. In this case, the optical spectrum in the long-period pulsation regime is accompanied by emission in three spectral regions with maximum at three wavelengths: 1562, 1598 and 1623 nm.

articleTitle: Highly strained InGaAs/GaAs quantum wells obtained by selective epitaxy
abstract: The results of experimental studies on semiconductor heterostructures with InGaAs quantum wells $\mathbf{(} \mathbf{9 8 0}-\mathbf{9 9 5 n m}$) grown by selective MOCVD epitaxy are presented. It is shown that the wavelength of photoluminescence varies across the window and depends on the thickness of the waveguide layer.

articleTitle: Generation of highly directional white light in airborne laser plasma
abstract: The experimental results of conditions study for formation of a highly directional supercontinuum in the visible region, which occurs during aberration focusing of radiation pulse with a wavelength of 940 nm and a duration of 70 fs are presented.

articleTitle: Pulsed laser annealing of sulfur hyperdoped silicon prepared by ion implantation
abstract: Silicon’s band gap ($\mathbf{1 . 1 2} \mathbf{~ e V}$) limits its near-infrared photon absorption. Silicon hyperdoping creates energy states within the band gap, enabling near-infrared radiation absorption. Ion implantation is an efficient method for hyperdoping, but radiation-induced defects compromise silicon crystallinity. Pulsed laser annealing mitigates induced defects, enhancing material crystallinity. The study investigates the impact of pulsed laser annealing on sulfur hyperdoped silicon properties prepared by ion implantation.

articleTitle: Raman spectroscopy as a tool for helicobacter pylori diagnostics
abstract: Raman spectroscopy was studied as a diagnostic tool for detecting Helicobacter pylori infection. We suggested a new methodology to account the changes in the spectrum of Raman scattering caused by pressure variations, which enabled us to measure the ${ }^{13} \mathrm{CO}_{2}$ fraction with a relative error $2.1 \%$. The results showed a positive correlation with a blood test for $\mathbf{H}$. pylori antibodies.

articleTitle: Helium-Xenon Gas-Discharge Fiber Laser
abstract: Operation of a 2.03-μm He-Xe gas-discharge fiber laser based on a hollow-core fiber and pumped by a microwave radiation at 2.45 GHz is investigated. Optimal gas-mixture composition and pressure are identified. Opportunities for further development of gas-discharge fiber lasers are discussed.

articleTitle: Gain-Switched Single-Frequency Y tterbium Fiber Laser
abstract: Wehave investigated the generation characteristics of a distributed Bragg reflector (DBR) short cavity ytterbium fiber laser. Due to pulse pumping, the laser with an emission wavelength of 1066 nm was operated in gain switch mode with pulse durations ranging from 32 ns to 83 ns.

articleTitle: Plasmonic photoconductive antennas based on Bi2-xSbxSeyTe3-y topological insulators
abstract: In this work, we present the first experimental observation of the enhanced THz radiation in plasmonic photoconductive antenna (PCA) based on $\mathrm{Bi}_{2-\mathrm{x}} \mathrm{Sb}_{\mathbf{x}} \mathrm{Se}_{\mathbf{y}} \mathrm{Te}_{3 \text {-y }}$ topological insulator (TI). By using numerical simulations, we optimized the plasmonic grating geometry to maximize optical light transmission, stimulating efficient surface plasmon-polariton (SPP) excitations along the TI/grating interface. We fabricated two equal PCAs, the one of which contains high-aspect ratio plasmonic grating. The THz spectral measurements showed a $\sim 9$-fold enhancement of the emitted THz power in the plasmonic TI-based PCA. The results of our study can open a pathway toward time-domain plasmonics-enhanced THz setups utilizing innovative photoconductive materials.

articleTitle: Thermally Induced Distortions of Radiation in Multipass Faraday Isolators
abstract: We investigated thermally induced depolarization in multi-pass Faraday isolators schemes, that are inevitable for low Verdet constant media. It is shown theoretically and experimentally that it is possible to increase isolation ratio 1.6 times by choosing the optimal distance between beams in “linear” arrangement and there is no optimum for the arrangement of beams along a circle.

articleTitle: Two Approaches to Estimate the Depth of Light Penetration into Biotissues
abstract: The depth to which light effectively penetrates biological tissues is still a matter of debate in photomedicine. The work compares two approaches to evaluate the depth, based, respectively, on the exponential decay, and on the estimation of a volume, where 95% of absorbed light is accumulated. It is shown that the approach, which uses the conventional exponential decay, underestimates the penetration depth in more than 2 times.

articleTitle: Semiconductor lasers in gain-switching mode for high power sub-ns optical pulses
abstract: Broad-arealasers with a $100 \ \mu \mathrm{m}$ aperture based on heterostructures with double asymmetry and active regions at wavelengths of 850 nm using bulk 45 nm GaAs and at 970 nm using quantum wells were investigated. Output optical powers in the single first relaxation peak regime from 12 to 22 W were achieved with pulse durations from 100 to 150 ps.

articleTitle: A model of the process of forming the optimal fractional composition of powders during compaction
abstract: A mathematical model for estimating the optimal fractional composition of the powder for compaction has been developing. The model has been testing on the data of fractional compositions of three mixtures. The laying of the powder mixture is modeling using the finite element method.

articleTitle: Estimation of a Time Dependent Frequency Shift of Whispering Gallery Modes due to The Pump Induced Heating
abstract: Numerical modeling and direct measurement of thermal frequency shift in microresonators was performed. Numerical results were compared with experimental data that provided information on methods accuracy. Thermal relaxation time and frequency shift of $\mathbf{M g F}_{2}$ microresonator was defined.

articleTitle: New mode of a steady-state superradiant lasing
abstract: We show that, for a wind range of parameters of a superradiant laser with a low-Q slightly asymmetric Fabry-Perot cavity, there is a strongly-asymmetric single-mode (narrow-line) lasing. It is defined by an inhomogeneous self-consistent half-wavelength population-inversion grating. We find analytically the universal profile of this grating and unusual profiles of the counter-propagating waves which form the grating and experience Bragg scattering by it. We outline the ways of control of the superradiant polariton mode and demonstrate its stability far above the lasing threshold.

articleTitle: Two-photon Absorption in Na2Mo2O7 Crystal Excited by Picosecond Pulses at 523 nm
abstract: Two-photon absorption was investigated in Na<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Mo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>anisotropic crystal under irradiation with picosecond laser pulses at 523 nm. The value of the coefficient of the two-photon absorption was measured to be 6.7 and $0.13 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{GW}$, depending on the orientation of the crystal.

articleTitle: Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering of Electrospun Nonwoven Fibers: Synthesis of Silver Nanoparticles and Their Effect on the Properties of SERS Materials
abstract: In this study, electrospun non-wovens were used as sensor templates. To functionalize the sensor surface, two ways were implemented: a one-step formation of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) on the surface of the material as a result of the ‘silver mirror’ reaction in situ, and a two-step procedure with preliminary synthesis of AgNPs and their subsequent implementation on the surface of nonwoven materials. The selected substrate was functionalized with an aqueous solution of the glucose oxidase enzyme (GOx). The resulting sensor can be used as a noninvasive high-specific glucose sensor in the composition of biological fluids.

articleTitle: Effect of liquid medium viscosity on laser cleaning of surface with artificial radioactive contamination
abstract: We present a cleaning method for stainless steel surfaces coated to simulate radioactive contamination. The simulated contamination was removed using laser radiation with a wavelength of 1 μm and pulse durations of 8 ns and 270 fs. For both gas and liquid environments, the most effective cleaning approaches were identified.

articleTitle: Optical properties of epitaxial InAs/GaAs quantum dots overgrown under different V/III flux ratios
abstract: We study the optical properties of InAs/GaAs(001) quantum dots (QDs) overgrown under different V/III flux ratios using photoluminescence (PL) and excitation spectroscopy. When the V/III flux ratio is low, a series of pronounced QD-related peaks is observed in the $77-\mathrm{K}$ PL spectrum over a $200-\mathrm{meV}$ broad spectral interval with the brightest one located at 1.37 eV. With increasing V/III flux ratio, the PL spectrum is red-shifted (to 1.16 eV) and then blue-shifted again (to 1.26 eV), while becoming smoother. We explain this behavior in terms of enhanced QD decomposition, the mechanism of which is different in cases of deficiency and excess of arsenic during the overgrowth.

articleTitle: Thermal Lens Measurement In LNM with Gerchberg-Saxton Algorhitm
abstract: Thermal lensing in LNM crystal was investigated with a technique, based on Gerchberg-Saxton algorithm. Aberrations of thermal lens, as well as its focal length were measured at 35 W of optical power, depending on the polarization of the incident light, with -0.32 m for one polarization, and more than 10 m thermal lens for the other orthogonal polarization.

articleTitle: Chlorophyll fluorescence parameters of maize plants grown under linearly polarized light
abstract: Chlorophyll fluorescence parameters were assessed for three Zea mays cv. grown under polarized light. It is shown that there was no stress in groups grown under polarized radiation. The greater values of photosynthetic parameters were observed in Early ripening gourmet 121 and Golden Batam cv. grown under polarized light in comparison with plants grown under non-polarized treatment.

articleTitle: Fast Spectroscopic Technique of Optical Biopsy of Intracranial Tumors
abstract: The possibility of differentiation of glial and meningeal tumors on the basis of the proposed method of optical-spectral analysis was shown. For non-fluorescing tumors, the most significant indicators were the intensity of elastic light scattering, carotenoid content, and the change in lipid/protein ratio.

articleTitle: Study of Migration of Elements on the Metal Surfaces after Laser Shock Peening in Water Medium
abstract: Paper describes the study of chemical composition of the metal surfaces after laser peening (shock hardening). The process of peening was implemented in air and water media. The special paints were tested as buffer layer, absorbing the destructive action of the laser radiation for providing stresses in material without surface deformation. Water media was used simultaneously for enforcement of shock action and for cooling. The element composition of surface layer after peening can differ to the same before laser treatment due to the physical and chemical processes in the zone of peening. Also, application of paints can facilitate their penetration into the surface layer. Laser induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) was applied for studying steel and aluminum alloys with different paints before and after laser shock peening in different modes.

articleTitle: Tapered fiber reinforcement for stable coupling with WGM microresonator
abstract: A method of the tapered fiber reinforcement for the stable coupling with whispering gallery mode (WGM) microresonator is developed. It is revealed that the slight curvature of tapered fiber results in its stronger fixation and prevents the sticking of the fiber and microresonator. An excitation of WGMs by reinforced curved tapered fiber with curvature radius about 15 mm is demonstrated experimentally.

articleTitle: PM Tm-doped fiber laser harmonically mode-locked using single-walled carbon nanotubes
abstract: A polarization maintaining thulium-doped fiber laser mode-locked by single-walled carbon nanotubes has been developed. The pulse repetition frequency varied with increasing power from 84 to 504 MHz. Following pulse parameters are achieved: the pulse duration of 440 fs, center wavelength of 1912 nm, maximum average power of 600 mW, maximum pulse energy of 1.2 nJ.

articleTitle: Single and Dual Wavelength Oscillation of Nd:YAG Laser at 1318 – 1444 nm
abstract: Pulsed oscillation of diode-side-pumped Nd:YAP laser with intracavity prism was studied. Single and dualwavelength oscillations at $1318.8,1338.2,1356.4,1414.0,1444.0$, $1318.8+1338.2,1338.2+1356.4 \mathrm{~nm}$ with output energy up to 350 mJ and slope efficiency of $6 \%$ was demonstrated.

articleTitle: High-power erbium-doped pulsed fiber laser for nonablative fractional photo-rejuvenation
abstract: We present a high-power erbium-doped all-fiber source that generates rectangular-shaped pulses with durations ranging from 200$\mu$s to 5 ms and pulse energies up to 130 mJ.The laser has a stable single-mode output, a compact size and was designed for fractional photorejuvenation procedures.

articleTitle: Experimental comparison of imaging photoplethysmography and laser speckle contrast imaging for blood flow assessment
abstract: In this work, responses of cortical vessels to the administration of a metabolic agent were measured in rats using contactless imaging photoplethysmography and laser speckle contrast imaging systems providing full field of view visualization of the blood flow. It was found that blood-flow changes detected by two systems differ significantly due to different nature of the interaction of light with tissues underlying these methods.

articleTitle: The effect of turbulent disturbances in entaglement-based quantum key distribution systems
abstract: In this paper, the possible negative effects of the influence of turbulent disturbances in atmospheric communication channels for entanglement-based quantum key distribution systems have been considered. In order to decrease these effects an active tracking system has been developed. We demonstrate the results of its evaluation in a quantum key distribution system.

articleTitle: Optical Multi-pass Cell for TDLAS Analysis of Human Breath
abstract: We conducted optical modeling and constructed a multi-pass optical cell for human breath analysis by Tunable Diode Laser Absorbtion Spectroscopy (TDLAS) techniques. The cell comprises two concave cylindrical mirrors and achieves a 3.5 m optical path length within a $5 \times 5 \times 5 \mathbf{c m}^{3}$ volume, enabling its use in portable devices for examining human exhalation.

articleTitle: New method for finding the temporal soliton at three waves interaction
abstract: New approach of obtaining the temporal soliton or soliton-like temporal structure at three waves interaction is proposed and demonstrated. It consists of two parts. In the first one, we construct the unchanged solution in long pulse duration approximation. In the second one, the condition of this solution stability to second order dispersion influence is derived.

articleTitle: A graded-index confined bismuth-doped fiber for cladding-pumped E+S-band high-power amplifiers
abstract: Amultimode double-clad graded-index fiber with the confined Bi -doped $\mathrm{GeO}_{2}-\mathrm{SiO}_{2}$ glass core was fabricated by all-gas-phase MCVD technology. The bismuth-doped fiber as an active medium exhibited good performance characteristics in the developed E+S-band power amplifier, which provided a maximum output power of about 1 W at an input signal of 150 mW under pumping by multimode laser diodes at 808 nm.

articleTitle: Near and Mid Infrared Channeled Waveguide Lasers in Rare-Earth Ion-Doped Fluoride Crystals
abstract: Femtosecond laser written waveguide lasers operating in the near and mid infrared region at 1318 nm and 2700-2800 nm were investigated by using $\mathrm{Nd}^{3+}: \mathrm{BaY}_{2} \mathrm{~F}_{8}$ and $\mathrm{Er}^{3+}:$ YiLF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> crystals.

articleTitle: Picosecond Nd:YAG laser for SLR in outdoor conditions
abstract: The design features of a high-frequency laser transmitter for SLR stations operating in a wide temperature range (from -50°C to +55°C) are reported. The laser generates pulses with a duration of 35 ps at a wavelength of 532 nm with a pulse energy of more than 2.5 mJ and a pulse repetition rate of at least 500 Hz.

articleTitle: Dissipative Phase Transition in quadratically driven Kerr Oscillator
abstract: The nonequilibrium dissipative phase transition of the Kerr oscillator with two-photon drive and dissipation is studied. We investigate properties of the steady state and critical slowing down near the phase transition point.

articleTitle: Microwave pumped multi-frequency planar (CO2-Xe)-laser
abstract: In a planar gas-discharge laser with microwave pumping and diffusion cooling of the working gas, lasing in the wavelength range $2-11 \mu \mathrm{m}$ was obtained simultaneously on xenon atoms and on carbon dioxide molecules. The output energy and spectral characteristics of the radiation of a pulse-periodic laser have been studied depending on: the composition and pressure of the working gas mixture; on the input power, on the duration and repetition rate of the pump pulses.

articleTitle: Coherent laser systems for remote atmosphere sensing
abstract: The paper studies the current trends in development of coherent laser systems as a radiation source in remote atmosphere sensing as well as precise ranging and data transfer through atmosphere or space. In the paper, a design of the coherent laser systems based on fiber technologies or another laser medium is presented. The paper also provides analysis of the technical requirements for laser components and discuss main parameters characterizes quality of emitted radiation.

articleTitle: Mode decomposition algorithm for enhancing the phase measurement accuracy
abstract: Holographic mode decomposition methods are extremely fruitful in revealing the physical mechanism of nonlinear effects, but also suffer from unresolved issues. In this work we improve the measurement accuracy of the relative modal phases, by adjusting the modal intensities.

articleTitle: Continuous dual-polarization signal processing using windowed Nonlinear Fourier Transform
abstract: We present a new way to handle dual-polarization signal processing in fiber-optic networks. It combines chromatic dispersion compensation (CDC) with sliding window techniques to make processing signals more precise and effective. The nonlinear Fourier transform (NFT) is a key tool used here to manage chromatic dispersion and the Kerr effect, which are crucial for transmitting signals over long distances.

articleTitle: Magnetic control of coherent tunneling in hybrid magnetic-dielectric integrated waveguides
abstract: Magnetic control of the light routing and transfer in the integrated planar waveguide structure that combined both magnetic and nonmagnetic waveguides on the silicon dioxide chip based on the coherent tunneling by adiabatic passage (CTAP) is addressed. It is shown that the CTAP effect can be realized in the waveguide structure made of quartz and iron-garnet waveguides. Introduction of the magnetic waveguide allows one to control the light transfer in the structure by means of the applied magnetic field. The effect is studied for two different directions of the external magnetic field.

articleTitle: Manufacturing of Optical Fibers for the Range of 4-27 ×m Based on Silver Halide Single Crystals
abstract: A technology has been developed for producing step-index fibers based on the AgBr-AgI system single crystals. The fiber cladding is made of $8 \mathrm{~mol}. \% \mathrm{AgI}$ in AgBr, core 12 mol. $\%$ AgI in AgBr. The fiber diameter was $1120 \mu \mathrm{m}$, core diameter $550 \mu \mathrm{m}$. The fiber is suitable for IR lasers and pyrometry.

articleTitle: High power photoactivated current switches for generating sub-ns electrical pulses
abstract: Photoactivated current switches for pumping diode laser stacks with ns and sub-ns current pulses are studied. Test optical pulse: 860 nm, 50 ps leading edge, peak power up to 9.3 W. Samples were tested at up to 50 V bias. Photoresponse amplitude was up to 17 V (340 mA) with linear dependence on pulse power. Photoresponse leading edge duration was ~80 ps (20-80% level).

articleTitle: Metrological assurance of frequency-stabilized lasers
abstract: The report is about the metrological assurance of frequency-stabilized lasers

articleTitle: Upconversion responsivity of 4F9/2-4I15/2 transition of erbium in NaYF4 matrix at high power pump
abstract: Inthis work is shown investigations the luminescence behavior of the erbium ${}^{4} \mathrm{~F}_{9 / 2}{}^{4} \mathrm{I}_{15 / 2}$ transition in a NaYF4 crystalline matrix doped with Yb and Er ions, over a wide range of pump power with a wavelength of 980 nm.

articleTitle: The Combined Use of Methylene blue and Chlorin E6 Photosensitizers for Photodynamic Therapy and Correction of the Tumor Microenvironement
abstract: In this work we report the results of the study of combined use of methylene blue with chlorin E6 photosensitizer for tumor oxygenation control and the tumor microenvironment correction during photodynamic therapy in vitro and in vivo. Targeted destruction of tumor-associated and synergistic effects due to the influence of methylene blue on tumor oxygenation were studied.

articleTitle: Time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy in differential diagnosis of liver cancer in vivo
abstract: Thiswork reports a machine-learning-based approach to interpret time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy data acquired during optical biopsy of the liver. The approach allowed to differentiate between liver parenchyma and tumor with sensitivity and specificity above 0.91 and 0.79, respectively, providing differential diagnosis of liver cancer (primary malignant tumor, metastases, or benign) with sensitivity and specificity of at least 0.80 and 0.95.

articleTitle: Beam self-cleaning and wave thermalization in multimode fibers
abstract: Spatial beam self-cleaning in multimode optical fibers may be described as a result of wave thermalization. Our mode decomposition experiments confirm the validity of this approach, but also point to open questions.

articleTitle: Research of the efficiency coupling of fiber laser radiation into a laminar water jet
abstract: This work examines the features of the process of propagation of laser radiation inside a water jet. The influence of beam parameters (Rayleigh length, focus position, number of aperture) on the loss of average power in a water jet is investigated. Different types of pulsed fiber lasers are considered.

Author Keywords: absorption of laser emitting by water

articleTitle: Laser Synthesis of Linear Carbon Structures for Nanophotonics
abstract: In this study, we investigate stable elongated carbon chains synthesized using the laser fragmentation technique in a colloidal solution. These chains are mechanically stabilized through the electron binding of the carbon chains to gold nanoparticles. Due to the high degree of alignment of gold-terminated carbyne chains, a strongly anisotropic light absorption is observed, characterized by a cosine dependence on the angle between the carbyne molecule and the polarization plane of excitation.

articleTitle: Stimulated Raman Scattering in Sodium Dimolybdate Crystal
abstract: Stimulated Raman scattering was obtained in anisotropic Na<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> Mo2 O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf> crystal with frequency shift of 37 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> when excited by picosecond pulses at wavelength of 1047 nm. Raman gain coefficient was measured depending on the orientation of the crystal.

articleTitle: Towards All-Fiber Chalcogenide System for Spectroscopic Remote Sensing in Mid-IR
abstract: Functionality of an analytical system on the base of chalcogenide fibers for remote mid-IR spectroscopy of liquids and gases in real time has been studied in theory and experiment.

articleTitle: High Thermal Tunability of Optical Transmission of Epsilon-Near-Zero Metamaterials Based on Nanorods in Liquid Crystals
abstract: We experimentally and numerically revealed a salient thermal effect in the transmission of the epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) metamaterial consisting of an array of plasmonic nanorods in a dielectric template. The flavor of the structure is freestanding nanorod segments surrounded by nematic liquid crystals possessing a strong thermal dependence of the anisotropic refractive index. The observed resonant enhancement of the thermal sensitivity of the transmission of this ENZ structure results from its nonlocal optical response giving rise to the zero-transmission effect, control over which is at the heart of our approach.

articleTitle: Incoherent source of laser radiation
abstract: A possibility is considered of a pulsed incoherent source of laser radiation on the basis of a mode-locked fibre laser. Incoherent laser radiation may consist of noise-like pulses, chirped pulses or chirped noise-like pulses. Different ways of generation regime implementation with suitable pulses are discussed.

articleTitle: Low-resolution realization of compressive sensing approach for low light photography based on spatial phase light modulator
abstract: Compressive sensing method is a widely used algorithm for shooting/capturing fast-moving objects as well as for low light photography. This paper looks into how the compressive sensing algorithm can be applied in a spatial phase light modulator. It demonstrates that a significant reduction in exposure time with no quality loss can be achieved.

articleTitle: Logic-Gate-Controlled Density of Antibody Binding Sites on Sensing Surface for Immunoassays with Improved Analytical Performance
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of balancing analytical performance (e.g., sensitivity, specificity, dynamic range) in the biosensing systems. Introducing a universal approach, we propose a surface with a molecularly controlled density of antibody binding sites using the molecular logic gate. Employing spectral interferometry, the ability to detect antibiotic chloramphenicol using glass sensor chips with adjustable density of biosensitive elements was experimentally demonstrated. This innovative approach offers controlled analytical characteristics for developing advanced systems to detect low-molecular-weight substances in areas such as food quality control, in vitro diagnostics, and veterinary medicine.

articleTitle: Wearable multimodal laser analyzers in assessing of microcirculatory disorders in the long COVID syndrome
abstract: The paper presents the results of the study of the effect of long COVID on the functional state of microcirculatorytissue systems of the human body using wearable multimodal laser analyzers.

articleTitle: FROG technique for the entangled soliton pulses identification
abstract: To use the entangled soliton pulses which can be produced via fission of the two-soliton breather in the optical fiber with periodically varying along the fiber dispersion in different applications such as quantum communications and quantum sensing the determination of entanglement between the pulses are necessary. The generated pulses are shifted symmetrically in carrier frequency to the red and to the blue according to the breather pulse. We propose to use the frequency resolved gating technique (FROG), when the signal pulse and reference pulses are combined at the nonlinear crystal for frequency sum generation. varying the delay of the pulses the spectrogram can be measured. The signal at the zero frequency corresponds to the signal and reference pulse interference. The FROG technique allows to measure the amplitude and the phase of the signal pulse.

articleTitle: Woofer-tweeter adaptive optical system for atmospheric turbulence mitigation
abstract: A woofer-tweeter approach is presented for compensation of the atmospheric turbulence negative effects. As a wavefront corrector for mitigation of the low-order aberrations with large amplitude the 23 -channel bimorph deformable mirror was used. To compensate for high-order aberrations with small amplitude the stacked-actuator deformable mirror with 55 control elements was exploited.

articleTitle: The Protocol of Quantum Key Distribution on Beams with Space Structured Polariztion
abstract: The work proposes a protocol for quantum key distribution using Laguerre-Gaussian beams with space structured polarization invariant to rotation of the radial coordinate in a plane normal to the beam propagation axis. It is shown that axial polarization symmetry makes such beams insensitive to rotations relative to the optical axis, which makes it possible to use them to transmit information in cryptographic protocols in space communication systems. Keywords: quantum key distribution; satellite-to-ground communications; vector beams with structured polarization; cube corner reflectors.

articleTitle: Singlet and Triplet Oxygen Detection by Time-correlated Single Photon Counting.
abstract: We present the technology, based on time-correlated single photon counting that enables molecular oxygen evaluation in biological samples, both in triplet and singlet states. In both cases, the measurements of phosphorescence signal is done. The measurement system is based on a hybrid and the superconducting single photon detector coupled to the confocal scanner that is modified for the near-infrared measurements.

articleTitle: Study of photo-oxidation of tetrahydrobiopterin with the addition of Pt-Pd nanoparticles
abstract: In the work, it was shown that the addition of platinum and palladium nanoparticle suspension promotes the formation of dihydropterin dimers when irradiated with ultraviolet light (325 nm) in the presence of oxygen.

articleTitle: Determination of the spectral dispersion for the heart muscle – a Kramers-Kronig approach
abstract: The refractive index of the pigs heart was measured at wavelengths between 255 and 850 nm to calculate the dispersion. The total transmittance and total reflectance spectra of the pig heart were measured between 200 and 1000 nm to calculate the spectral absorption coefficient. Using Kramers-Kronig relations, the dispersion of the heart was matched to experimental refractive index values.

articleTitle: Laser Beam Structure Influence on Optical and Structural Modification of Phase-Change Materials
abstract: Phase-change materials allow rapid and reversible switching between the optically different amorphous and crystalline phases. The transitions of amorphous $\mathrm{Ge}_{2} \mathbf{S b}_{2} \mathrm{Te}_{5}$ to the crystalline state as a result of exposure to various structured cw laser beams were studied. For cw irradiation this transition is related to heating above the crystallization temperature. Laser beams with an annular intensity profile have been shown to be more attractive for photoinduced crystallization of $\mathbf{G e}_{2} \mathbf{S b}_{2} \mathbf{T e}_{5}$ crystallization compared to the Hermite-Gaussian $\mathbf{H G}_{00}\left(\mathbf{T E M}_{00}\right)$ mode due to a more uniform temperature distribution within the irradiated region. Optical microscopy, Raman spectroscopy and the numerical simulations confirm higher crystallization efficiency of the cylindrical beams.

articleTitle: Analysis of the thermal resistance of high-power semiconductor lasers based on Al-containing and Al-free heterostructures.
abstract: This work is devoted to the computational analysis of high-power CW and QCW semiconductor laser sources in the spectral range 810-980 nm based on Al-containing and Al-free heterostructures.

articleTitle: Low-Order Harmonics Generation by Atoms and Asymmetric Molecules in Static Electric Field and Intense Laser Pulse
abstract: We derive analytical formulas for the free-electron current density excited during gas tunneling ionization in laser field in the presence of the static electric field. The amplitudes of generated low-order harmonics are compared with the results of the numerical calculations based on solving the time-dependent Schrödinger equation for hydrogen and helium atoms and time-dependent Kohn-Sham equations for oriented CO and HCl molecules. We find the ranges of parameters corresponding to the dominance of the ionization mechanism of even harmonics generation. These parameters can be used for high-resolved sampling detection of terahertz and mid-infrared pulses.

Author Keywords: detection of THz and mid-IR radiation

articleTitle: Femtosecond Laser-Induced Periodic Surface Structures Formation on optical fibers
abstract: Highly regular thermochemical laser-induced periodic surface structures (TLIPSS) were produced on the thin Ti metal film deposited on a curved side surface of optical fiber using femtosecond IR laser pulses. The significant dependence of structures regularity on the laser polarization direction relative to the fiber axis was revealed. Results of TLIPSS formation on fiber tip and their practical applications are presented.

articleTitle: Lyapunov Exponents Approach to Creating Ring Fiber Cavity Regime Charts
abstract: Lyapunov exponents method is used to unambiguously determine the dynamical state of the ring fiber cavity systems. Two-dimensional charts are then created to provide visual representation of the areas in given phase space, which clearly demonstrate how a certain nonlinear effect or instability in the cavity depends on its physical parameters. Mode prediction probability using the obtained charts is discussed.

articleTitle: Optoacoustic Effects On Laser Breakdown In A Liquid
abstract: The work is devoted to the study of acoustic effects accompanying a laser breakdown in a liquid. The connection between optical breakdown thresholds and acoustic cavitation thresholds has been established. It is shown that the combined optical and ultrasonic effects reduce cavitation thresholds and enhance the intensity of the illuminated spectral lines of chemical elements during laser breakdown in the presence of ultrasound.

articleTitle: Silver nanoparticles for therapy HER2-positive breast cancers
abstract: Cancer is one of the most challenging diseases. Despite the rapid development of medicine, cancer remains one of the main causes of death today. Women continue to have the highest incidence specifically of breast cancer. The resistance of cancer cells to chemotherapy is a major factor contributing to the limited success of conventional cancer treatments. Consequently, there is widespread global research aimed at devising more potent treatment strategies, including the exploration of nanomaterials for precise and targeted action against cancer cells.

articleTitle: High-contrast gratings for multispectral laser sources based on III-V/SOI photonic integrated circuits
abstract: A computational study of high-contrast gratings (HCG) in a vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL) on silicon-on-insulator (SOI) for multispectral laser sources is performed. The simulation model analyzes reflectivity of the HCG grating, formed in the SOI device layer. HCG filters higher-order modes, optimizing VCSEL performance. An algorithm is developed to determine HCG parameters, maximizing reflectivity with a SOI silicon layer fixed thickness.

articleTitle: High-temperature continuous terahertz laser discharge at NovoFEL: parameters and applications
abstract: A stable point-like thermodynamically-equilibrium plasma with diameter of 1 mm, density of $3 \times 10^{17}$ $\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$, and temperature of 4-4.5 $\mathrm{eV}(\mathbf{4 6 0 0 0 - 5 2 0 0 0 ~ K})$ was obtained in a continuous Kr- N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser discharge at NovoFEL at an average radiation power of less than 200 W. Such plasma is a bright source of VUV radiation, and when its temperature reaches $10-12$ eV, it can be a bright source of EVUV radiation, necessary for modern photolithography.

Author Keywords: point-like source of VUV and EVUV radiation

articleTitle: Mid IR Fiber Lasers based on Rare Earth Ions doped Chalcogenide Glasses
abstract: We demonstrate chalcogenide glass fiber lasers emitting at $4.6-5.4 \mu \mathrm{m}$. The fibers had $\boldsymbol{\emptyset} 20 \mu \mathrm{m}$ selenide core with of $\mathbf{T b}^{3+}$ or $\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}$ doping and undoped $\boldsymbol{\varrho} 240-250 ~ \mu \mathrm{m}$ sulfide cladding. The 200 and 7 mW output power with 8 and $17 \%$ slope efficiency was obtained for $\mathrm{Tb}^{3+}$ - and $\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}$-doped fibers respectively.

articleTitle: Dynamics of lasing switching between the ground and excited-state in a quantum-dot microdisk
