abstract: The work is devoted to the preparation of a luminescent crystalline substance based on $\mathrm{AgBr}_{0.8} \mathrm{I}_{0.2}: \mathrm{NdCl}_{3}$ and obtaining its luminescence spectra.

articleTitle: Dynamic of absorption spectra of biologically active substances of Tagetes erecta L. flowers extract in the visible wavelength region
abstract: In this work, spectral studies of marigold flower extract have been carried out. The extraction was prepared by maceration method. The triglycerides of fatty acids were used as an extractant. The resulting extract was diluted and the absorption spectra were measured.

articleTitle: Temperature-dependence of spectral and kinetic characteristics of 8.3(3) at. % Yb: YSAG laser ceramics
abstract: Spectral and kinetic characteristics of 8.3(3) at. % Yb:YSAG laser ceramics produced by sintering solid solution powders have been studied at different temperatures.

articleTitle: Cryothermal Setup for Arctic Fiber Bragg Grating Tilt Sensors Investigation
abstract: We propose a new cryothermal setup for testing and comparison fiber optic tilt sensors in extremely-low temperature conditions. The setup makes possible simulating the required temperature conditions, investigating fiber optic tilt sensors accuracy characteristics and tracing trends of the sensors operation when ambient temperature decreases to critical low values.

articleTitle: Preparation and Optical Properties of Transparent Spinel-Based Glass-Ceramics Containing Fe(II) Ions
abstract: Transparent glass-ceramics of magnesium, lithium-gallium, lithium, and zinc aluminosilicate systems based on $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}-$ doped nanosized $(4-20 \mathrm{~nm}$) crystals with spinel structure are developed by secondary heat-treatments of glasses melted in reducing conditions using TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> or a mixture of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and ZrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> as nucleating agents. Their structure and optical properties are studied. The prepared glass-ceramics are promising as saturable absorbers for lasers operating at $\sim 2 \mu \mathrm{m}$.

articleTitle: Site-controlled Ga(Al)As nanostructure arrays emitting at 740 nm
abstract: We presents the results of experimental studies of the formation processes and optical properties of ordered arrays of Ga(Al)As nanostructures on $\mathrm{GaAs}(\mathbf{0 0 1})$ substrates with regular arrays of pyramidal-shaped holes. The possibility AIGaAs solid solution on a structured surface decomposes with the formation of low-dimensional structures enriched by the Ga component is demonstrated. We have also shown that the emission wavelength $(740 \mathbf{n m})$ of site-controlled Ga(Al) As nanostructures is practically independent of the patterned surface morphology, while the emission intensity is determined by the effective volume of nanostructures.

articleTitle: Pockels cells on RTP crystals for for high-peak and medium power picosecond Nd:YAG laser systems
abstract: Pockels cells on domestic high-resistance RTP crystals with a contrast of at least 1000:1 for Nd:YAG lasers has been developed. The use of manufactured Pockels cells in a picosecond Nd:YAG laser made it possible to obtain the following characteristics of the generation pulses: a repetition frequency of 500 Hz, a duration of 35 ps, and a maximum energy of 4.2 mJ.

articleTitle: Coherent and incoherent scattering a counter-propagating laser pulse at a relativistic electron mirror
abstract: Using two-dimensional numerical simulations, interaction of a counter-propagating probe laser pulse with a relativistic electron mirror formed with an accelerating laser from a plasma layer is investigated. It is shown that both coherent and incoherent parts in the scattered radiation can be formed and their characteristics are studied. The incoherent radiation frequency can be considerably larger than that for the coherent part.

Author Keywords: interaction of laser radiation with matter
laser pulse scattering off relativistic electron mirror

articleTitle: Sapphire THz waveguides for sensing and endoscopy applications
abstract: THz technologies developments into practice are limited by the absence of commercially available THz endoscopic systems. Previously, the transmission properties of waveguides, fibers and even fiber bundles based on shaped sapphire were studied. Sapphire hollow-core waveguides are suitable for efficient radiation transmission with minimal losses and for applications in endoscopy of hard-to-access objects and highresolution imaging.

articleTitle: Nanocomposite coatings to improve the hemocompatibility of medical devices
abstract: This paper presents a method for the formation of nanocomposite hemocompatible coatings based on carbon nanotubes (CNTs) in a collagen polymer matrix using laser radiation. A microfluidic system was developed as a tool for in vitro testing of the coatings under dynamic flow conditions. Optical profilometry and Raman spectroscopy were used to evaluate the stability and hemocompatibility of the fabricated coatings.

articleTitle: Studying thermal effects of infrared femtosecond laser pulses applied for laser assisted hatching procedure on mouse embryos
abstract: Infrared femtosecond laser pulses are used for microsurgery of zona pellucida of mouse embryos at late stages of preimplantation development. Safety of the procedure is studied through embryo viability and heat shock proteins (HSP) gene expression assessment methods. Expression levels of HSP90 were shown to increase slightly compared to the negative control group suggesting delicacy of the femtosecond microsurgery.

articleTitle: Filters Based on Taped Optical Fibers 1.2 – 1.6 μm
abstract: This work presents the development and analysis of tunable spectral filters using tapered fibers. The filter was created by heating and pulling single mode optical fiber to form tapers. The optical signal propagating in the fiber within the 1.2 to $1.6 \mu \mathrm{m}$ range was filtered by bending the taper.

articleTitle: Optical fuse as a countermeasure against light injection attacks on quantum key distribution systems
abstract: In this paper, we propose an original device that can protect quantum key distribution (QKD) systems from the effects of intense laser radiation. Carbon nanomaterials dispersed in a polymer can be used as a fuse for QKD systems.

Author Keywords: protection of quantum key distribution systems (QKD)

articleTitle: The fs-laser inscription of fiber Bragg gratings based on spatial light modulator
abstract: We proposed a flexible approach for femtosecond laser based FBGs writing in optical fibers assisted by a spatial light modulator to set the position of focal point inside the fiber core. Uniform, phase-shifted, apodized FBGs were demonstrated using this technique. Moreover, we present capability of grating pitch transverse dimension change from a single point to the more complex shapes showing truly 3D structuring of refractive index inside the bulk of transparent materials.

articleTitle: Axially Symmetric Hermite-Gaussian Beams for the Space-Earth Quantum Cryptography Channel
abstract: The work provides a description of Hermite Gaussian beams with an axially symmetric polarization structure. It is shown that the axial polarization symmetry makes such beams insensitive to the rotations relative to the optical axis. That property makes such beams preferred for the quantum space communication and cryptography systems. The possible creation and detection of such beams within the framework of a polarization coding protocol is discussed.

articleTitle: Effect of collisions and optical pumping on the shape of magnetic resonance
abstract: In this work we investigate the form of magnetic resonance in gas cells with alkali metal atoms and buffer gas depending on the parameters of the laser pumping. The influence of collision effects such as quenching and breaking the hyperfine interaction on optical pumping and the shape of magnetic resonance is studied. These studies have application in optical magnetometers.

articleTitle: Optimization of degenerate four-wave mixing threshold parameters in dual-pumped microresonator
abstract: The numerical and analytical analyses were conducted to determine the optimal parameters of a bichromatically pumped microring resonator system, focusing on the generation process of squeezed light states.

articleTitle: Subthreshold electroluminescence from long-side-cleaved quantum-cascade laser
abstract: The room temperature subthreshold electroluminescence of $8 \mu \mathrm{m}$ quantum-cascade lasers grown by molecular-beam epitaxy is measured and analyzed.

articleTitle: Plasmonic sensors for detection of protein aging in solution
abstract: The aging process of proteins and protein based drugs is accompanied by their oxidation and the formation of post-translational modifications (PTMs) and, as a consequence, a change in their functional properties. Due to the oxidation of organic biomolecules, heterogeneous systems of fluorophores are formed that have a fluorescent response in the visible and near-infrared regions of the spectrum. Sensitive methods are required to detect such near-infrared emission. The use of plasmonic sensors to amplify and detect such a signal is potentially a promising method for routine analysis due to its sensitivity, simple and inexpensive equipment, and minimal sample preparation. This work examines the possibility of using plasmonic sensors to monitor the fluorescence of proteins during their aging process.

articleTitle: Validation and comparative analysis of off-axis digital holographic microscopy and SLIM for biological applications
abstract: Off-axis digital holographic microscopy with illumination by a coherent He-Ne laser and spatial light interference microscopy (SLIM) with partially coherent illumination were implemented and validated on a test object composed of polystyrene beads dissolved in water. Phase imaging of the test object using SLIM technique was performed using two illumination patterns: an annular ring condenser aperture and small circular condenser aperture.

articleTitle: New multipass telescopic scheme design for a multi-element disk laser amplifier
abstract: A new telescopic multipass scheme for a high energy multi-element disk laser amplifier with image transferring from AE to AE is proposed. The possibility of scaling the system to required number of elements was confirmed with the pilot source. Yb:YAG amplifier with two disc AEs and two 2.5 kW pumps is assembled and ready for testing.

articleTitle: Photoluminescent aerogels with RGB emission
abstract: Three new luminescence aerogels based on silica matrix and $\beta$-diketone complex with Eu(III) and 8- hydroxyquinoline complexes with Al(III) and Ca(II) have been synthesized and investigated. The obtained aerogels had PL maxima in the red, green, and blue regions of the visible range, respectively.

articleTitle: The effect of optical clearing agents on the results obtained with the digital nailfold capillaroscopy
abstract: In this work, the influence of optical clearing agents (OCA) on the blood flow in nailfold capillaries was studied. It was shown that parameters obtained by nailfold capillaroscopy technique depend on OCAs used for the visualization of capillaries.

articleTitle: Side-band modes in open optical resonators of pulse-periodic free electron lasers
abstract: In pulse-periodic free electron lasers in which the axes of the pump (electron beam) and an optical resonator with certain geometric parameters do not coincide, the hyperfine mode structure of the radiation consists not only of the classical super-modes (comb systems of longitudinal modes), but also of additional modes at side-band frequencies. The physical basis for generation of such modes is described with examples of optical resonators of the Novosibirsk free electron laser (NovoFEL).

articleTitle: Confined Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering for Bio-objects Detection
abstract: An analytical theory and experiments are proposed to study surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) from molecules located inside a hollow metal resonator. The EM mechanism is considered for the confined SERS. Raman scattering measured from bare as well as from silver-coated polystyrene spheres is consistent with our theory of the confined SERS.

articleTitle: Singlet oxygen generation by Radachlorin photosensitizer in albumin-containing solutions
abstract: We present experimental analysis of singlet oxygen (SO) generation by Radachlorin photosensitizer (PS) in solutions with human serum albumin (HSA) at different relative concentrations of PS and HSA. The gradual decrease of the SO phosphorescence signal with rising amount of albumin molecules has been observed and interpreted.

articleTitle: Time-varying polarization measurements of ultrashort pulses at 1.9 μm based on GRENOUILLE
abstract: Time-dependent polarization measurements of ultrashort pulses at $1.9 \mu \mathrm{m}$ from a thulium-doped fiber laser system adjustable with polarization controllers were demonstrated. The measurements are based on the GRENOUILLE device and the TURTLE method. By adjusting the polarization controllers of the laser system, a variety of time-polarization pulses were obtained, some of them were characterized.

articleTitle: New approach of non-coherent power scaling of fiber sources for material processing
abstract: A new method of a few fiber laser sources combining is proposed: using a single bulk termination with a multiply fiber inputs. A practical implementation of multi-channel pulsed fiber laser for surface cleaning application was demonstrated.

articleTitle: Influenza A Virus Detection via Ag@c-Si SERS and Machine Learning
abstract: Thisstudy demonstrates the efficacy of surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) combined with machine learning for detecting and distinguishing influenza A virus in an STE buffer medium. Dendritic Ag structures on single-crystal silicon were proposed as SERS-active substrates, synthesized via a costeffective method yielding varied morphologies. Spectroscopic ellipsometry aided in substrate selection based on optical properties, with the most promising substrate exhibiting a localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) near the excitation wavelength. SERS analysis before and after viral exposure revealed subtle spectral differences, necessitating machine learning algorithms for accurate classification, achieving a detection accuracy of $76.6 \pm 4.2 \%$.

articleTitle: Methylene blue-mediated photodynamic therapy and tissue oxygen saturation control of postoperative mammary gland scars
abstract: Wounds are major health care problem. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is a non-invasive procedure, can be applied to stimulate healing of skin wounds resulting from mammary gland surgery. The development of approach to treatment of postoperative scars with PDT and simultaneous tissue oxygen saturation control will reduce the time of tissue healing and decrease the incidence of postoperative scars inflammation.

Author Keywords: diffuse scattering spectroscopy in visible range

articleTitle: Measurement of optical absorption coefficient of lithium-sodium molybdate crystals
abstract: We introduce the measurement results of the optical absorption coefficient of the lithium-sodium molybdate nonlinear-optical crystal at 1070 nm wavelength.

articleTitle: Fiber Pyrometer Based on AgCl0.25Br0.75 - AgI Fiber for Measuring Temperature in Hard-to-Reach Places
abstract: Thework is devoted to the manufacture of a fiber pyrometer based on AgCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.25</inf>Br<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.75</inf> - AgI fibers and using it to measure the temperature of objects in the range of $36-50^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$

articleTitle: PECVD-fabricated microresonators for nonlinear photonics
abstract: We demonstrate characteristics of high-Q ring silicon nitride microresonators fabricated with novel PECVD process. Proposed process allows to fabricate silicon nitride waveguides with thickness over 1 um. Studied 1um-thick silicon nitride ring microresontors features anomalous GVD and loaded Q factor over 1 million.

articleTitle: Spectral and Energy Characteristics of Picosecond SRS in Heavy Water
abstract: The forward and backward stimulated Raman scattering (FSRS, BSRS) in heavy water was studied when excited by the second harmonic radiation of a picosecond (60 ps) Nd:YAG laser. Generation was obtained in the Stokes region at 5 wavelengths in the spectral range of 566 – 723 nm and in the anti-Stokes region at 4 wavelengths in the spectral range of 427 - 474 nm. The maximum energy efficiency of SRS conversion reached 5%.

articleTitle: Infrared Fibers Based on AgCl – AgBr0.7I0.3 for Medical and Laser Technologies
abstract: For medical laser technologies, IR fibers based on single crystals of the $\mathbf{A g C l}-\mathrm{AgBr}_{0.7} \mathbf{I}_{0.3}$ system have been developed. Using computer simulation, extrusion modes were determined and fibers with a diameter of $465 \mu \mathrm{m}$ and a length of 1.4 m were obtained. They have a transmission range of 3.4-24.0 $\mu \mathrm{m}$ without absorption windows and low optical losses.

articleTitle: Development of a New Crystalline Scintillation Single Crystal Based on Silver and Thallium Halides
abstract: A new scintillation single crystal based on silver and monovalent thallium halides for scintillation optics has been designed, synthesized and studied for the detection and measurement of ionizing radiation.

articleTitle: Electron accelerator driven by 1TW femtosecond laser pulses: targetry, principles and prospects
abstract: Various methods and approaches of efficient bunched high energy particles accelerations are discussed with the use of few terawatt-class lasers interacting with tailored under-critical plasma.

articleTitle: 11dB SBS-gain suppressed Al2O3/GeO2/P2O5/F-doped silica LMA optical fiber for high-power singlefrequency radiation delivery
abstract: A new design of a passive large mode area (LMA) optical fiber with record (for such type of fibers) stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) gain suppression, no less than 11dB compared to a conventional LMA fiber, is reported. The fiber core consists of two parts: the central, doped with Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and GeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and the peripheral, doped with P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> and F, which creates the Brillouin gain spectrum (BGS) spread by 1 GHz. The SBS properties were confirmed by BGS and SBS power threshold measurements.

articleTitle: New Fast Exponential Splitting Schemes for Nonlinear Fourier Transform
abstract: The nonlinear Fourier transform (NFT) is a method for analyzing signal structures influenced by the nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLSE). Enhancing the performance and accuracy of NFT algorithms is crucial in fiber optics. We propose a method to identify all suitable symmetric exponential splitting schemes that enhance the speed of fast NFT (FNFT) algorithms while maintaining low numerical complexity. The schemes we developed performed well in numerical tests, comparing favorably with other fast 4th order NFT algorithms.

articleTitle: Ultrafine Precursor for Laser Sintering of Er:YAG – 20Bi2O3-60B2O3-20BaO Glass Ceramics
abstract: A method has been developed for producing an amorphous ultrafine precursor with different ratios of Er:Y AG and $20 \mathrm{Bi}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}-60 \mathrm{~B}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}-20 \mathrm{BaO}$. The method of selective laser sintering has been used to demonstrate the possibility of forming functional glass ceramics with a crystalline phase represented by yttrium aluminum garnet and yttrium/erbium borate.

articleTitle: Clinical and immunologic results of photodynamic therapy for HPV-associated cervical diseases
abstract: Chlorine E6 photodynamic therapy (PDT) was used to treat 183 patients with HPV-related cervical diseases. The main of this study was to characterize the local immune response during treatment with PDT in patients with persistent HPV infection, LSIL, HSIL and cervical cancer. PDT is able to stimulate antiviral innate immune response, being important to treatment effectiveness.

articleTitle: The method for the investigation of wavefront distortion in laser amplifiers
abstract: The method of laser scanning is proposed and developed for the investigation of radiation wavefront distortion in active elements of high-power laser amplifiers. Optical path difference profile is calculated from simultaneously investigated temperature and inverted population distributions in an active element. Optical path difference profiles introduced by pumped active elements of high-power laser amplifier are studied.

articleTitle: Second-harmonic generation in LiNa5Mo9O30 crystalline sample
abstract: Second-harmonic generation (SHG) of 1030 nm wavelength was performed in lithium-sodium molybdate crystal. The dependences of both SHG power and conversion efficiency on pump power were measured.

articleTitle: Enhanced Chemiluminescence of Luminol by Silver and Gold Nanoparticles: Investigating the Role of Particle Size, Shape, and Concentration
abstract: The influence of the shape and size of silver and gold nanoparticles on the chemiluminescence of luminol was studied. To create metal nanoparticles, colloidal synthesis, and the method of pulsed laser ablation in liquid were used. It was found that when a certain amount of metal nanoparticles was added, the chemiluminescence intensity of luminol also increased, and this effect was observed at different pH levels. In addition, it has been shown that the shape of silver and gold nanoparticles also affects the chemiluminescence intensity.

articleTitle: Measurement of covariance of analog detector readings in the field of spontaneous parametric down-conversion
abstract: An approach is considered that can be applied to calibrate detectors operating in the analog signal recording mode. Statistical distributions of the readings of such detectors are studied taking into account fluctuations in the amplitudes of single-photon detector pulses.

articleTitle: Visible light communication system based on RGBW LEDs
abstract: This study introduces a duplex Li-Fi communication system that utilizes the red color of RGBW LED for data transmission. The system demonstrated an Internet connection data rate of up to $42 \mathrm{Mbit} / \mathrm{s}$ at 4 meters between the master and slave modules.

articleTitle: Photon Antibunching as a Tool for Enhancement of Nanosensors Spatial Resolution
abstract: We propose a method of spatial resolution enhancement in metrology (magnetometry, thermometry, pH estimation and similar methods) with color center based nanosensors by taking into account photon antibunching for single quantum emitters. Numerical simulations demonstrate efficiency of the approach. We perform quantitative estimation of the image information increase due to exploitation of photon antibunching and find the conditions, under which application of the proposed method is reasonable.

articleTitle: Energy relaxation in a strongly excited electron subsystem of a Nickel film on a substrate
abstract: Non-destructive and non-contact all-optical methods for characterization of thermal and mechanical properties of layered materials with nanoscale spatial and femtosecond/picosecond temporal resolutions are in ever-increasing demand. Here, we report on an experimental study of energy relaxation in a strongly excited electron subsystem of a Nickel film on a substrate upon irradiation with an ultrashort laser pulse using time-resolved pump-probe reflectivity measurements with phase-sensitive signal detection. The temporal dynamics of changes in reflectivity at initial electron temperatures reaching several thousand kelvins contains essential information about the ultrafast electron relaxation, electron-phonon coupling parameter, electron thermal conductivity and heat capacitance of the metal film, as well as elastic and mechanical properties revealed by detection of propagating picosecond coherent acoustic phonons in the gigahertz frequency range both in the metal and substrate. We believe these experimental data to be useful for validation of the theories existing at present time and the further development of predictive modelling.

articleTitle: Interferometric reconstruction of the complex amplitude (IRCA) of femtosecond pulses
abstract: A novel femtosecond diagnostic technique based on interferometric reconstruction of the complex amplitude (IRCA) of the E-field is introduced. It employs same-scan acquisitions of the Michelson interferometer signal along with the fringe-resolved autocorrelation function (ACF). Fourier transform spectrometry is used to evaluate optical pulse spectrum. Once the pulse spectrum and ACF are known, the pulse E-field is calculated. Such approach greatly simplifies hardware, reduces its mechanical dimensions and costs.

articleTitle: Water transportation across membrane aquaporin channels by monomer H2O : 20 anniversary Peter Agre Nobel Prize
abstract: P.Agre (Nobel Prize, 2003) said that water transportation across membrane aquaporin channel by monomer H2O occurs with intensity around 3E9 monomer/s. It’s still unknown till now where this monomer amount may storage? We have observed that water-air interface layer consists of a two water fraction: it has high/low meniscus height when capillary touch the surface/bulk water. Keywords - membrane, H2O monomer transpotaion by aquaporin channel, ortho-para spin isomers of H2O

articleTitle: MBE growth and properties of III-V hybrid nanostrucres on silicon for quantum applications
abstract: InGaAs quantum dots in AlGaAs nanowires were formed using molecular-beam epitaxy on the silicon surface for the first time. The dependence of the synthesized nanostructures physical properties on growth conditions was studied. The results of optical properties studies showed that photoluminescence spectra from InGaAs quantum dots are observed at room temperature in a wide range of wavelengths from 850 to 1300 nm. Based on experimental data, modeling of the optical properties of the synthesized nanostructures was carried out.

articleTitle: Experimental reservoir computing based on a laser subject to optoelectronic feedback
abstract: We experimentally study a reservoir computing system based on a DFB laser diode with positive optoelectronic feedback. The system is operated in the vicinity of the Hopf bifurcation at 40 MHz input symbol rate. We evaluate memory capacity of the system and a chaotic time series prediction error.

articleTitle: Cerebral Blood Flow Dynamics in Rats with Blood Loss
abstract: This paper presents the results of investigating the blood flow dynamics using the laser speckle contrast imaging method in rats with blood loss and without it. The results indicate that under such conditions, there was no significant decrease in speckle perfusion values.

articleTitle: Raman dissipative soliton parameters near 1.7 microns depending on external cavity dispersion
abstract: In this paper, we have studied a Raman dissipative solitons (RDS) oscillator at a wavelength near 1.7 microns with external cavity pumping from an erbium doped mode-locked laser. It was numerically simulated in various configurations to investigate the effects of dispersion management on the pulse characteristics and modes of operation.

articleTitle: Formation and dynamic parameters of light-induced microcavities in a resonant medium
abstract: In this talk, the formation and control of optical microcavities by the collision of unipolar light pulses in resonant media is theoretically demonstrated.

articleTitle: Interference of radiation at fundamental and tripled frequencies with superbroadening of the few-cycle pulse spectrum in nonlinear media
abstract: In media with cubic nonlinearity, broadening of the optical pulses’ spectrum is observed due to their phase modulation and generation of radiation at triple frequencies. When the number of oscillations in the original pulse is small, these spectra may overlap, resulting in unconventional phenomena for traditional nonlinear optics such as mutual amplification or attenuation effects of phase modulation and generation of radiation at triple frequencies, which are nonuniform across the spectrum. The report discusses the theory of these phenomena and presents the results of their experimental observations in the terahertz spectral range.

articleTitle: Growth and Polarized Spectroscopy of Stoichiometric NaEu(WO4)2 Laser Crystal
abstract: Stoichiometric tetragonal disordered $\mathrm{NaEu}\left(\mathrm{WO}_{4}\right)_{2}$ laser crystal is grown by the Czochralski method and its polarized spectroscopic properties are studied. The stimulate-demission cross-section for the deep-red ${ }^{5} \mathrm{D}_{0} \rightarrow{ }^{7} \mathrm{~F}_{4}$ transition is $2.53 \times 10^{-20} \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$ at $\sim 702 \mathrm{~nm}$ for $\pi$-polarization.

articleTitle: H3 diamond color centers for quantum magnetometry
abstract: For the first time, we demonstrated the sensitivity of diamond H3 color centers to a magnetic field. The diamond H3 color centers represent the neutral charge state of the $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{V}-\mathrm{N}$ centers, i.e. two donor electrons are localized in the vacancy from nitrogen atoms included in the center structure. This suggests the spin splitting of the electronic states of the H3 center into spin sublevels. Thus, H 3 (or $\mathrm{N}_{2} \mathrm{~V}^{0}$) diamond color centers may be used in quantum sensors and, possibly, in quantum computing.

articleTitle: Parallel beam pumped picosecond Raman laser on water with a preamplifier
abstract: We report the observation of stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) in water when excited by non-focused beam of a picosecond (15 ps) pulsed Nd:YLF laser second harmonic (527 nm). In the experiments, a set of cylindrical cuvettes of different lengths has been used. The SRS generation has been achieved when the laser pulse optical path length in the sample reached a certain value. Such experimental setup can be considered as a SRS laser with a preamplifier pumped by a parallel beam.

articleTitle: Temperature dependences of light emission and energy transfer in heterostructures with CdTe quantum wells of various thicknesses
abstract: Understanding the mechanisms of energy transfer between the elements of heterostructures used in optoelectronics is essential for optimizing the design of the devices. This problem is being actively studied at various types of objects [1–4]. The transfer of excitons and carriers as well as the dipole-dipole FÖrster type transfer [5] are possible.

articleTitle: Spectroscopy of thulium ions in novel oxychloride lead-tellurite glasses
abstract: Thulium-doped oxychloride lead-tellurite glasses were synthesized, and their spectroscopic properties were studied focusing on $\mathrm{Tm}^{3+}$ emissions at $2-3 \mu \mathrm{m}$. $\mathrm{Tm}^{3+}$ ions exhibit relatively long luminescence lifetimes of the ${ }^{3} \mathrm{H}_{4}$ and ${ }^{3} \mathrm{~F}_{4}$ states owing to the low-phonon-energy behavior of the glass matrix.

articleTitle: Glasses with I-VII and II-VI semiconductor nanocrystals for nonlinear optical limiting
abstract: The spectral properties of inorganic glasses with I-VII and II-VI nanocrystals and quantum dots are investigated. Nanosized copper halide and cadmium chalcogenide crystals stabilized in glass matrix are shown to be a perspective material for nonlinear optical limiting.

articleTitle: Status report on modification of JINR UV laser for generating relativistic vortex electrons
abstract: ITMO-JINR multidisciplinary project: development of the source of relativistic vortex electrons (carrying orbital angular momentum - OAM) based on the LINAC-200 electron accelerator in JINR. First stage: testbench with RF-gun based acceleration yielding vortex electrons with energies up to 5 MeV. Concept: generating vortex electrons via photoemission process with OAM transfer from photons to electrons.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo Modeling of the Red Blood Cell Aggregation in Photoplethysmography
abstract: The effect of red blood cell (RBC) aggregation on the photoplethysmography (PPG) signal at a wavelength of 810 nm was investigated using the Monte Carlo method. It was found that the main contribution to the formation of the PPG signal is made by scattering variations due to changes in the rouleaux size ($84 \%$ versus $16 \%$ absorption, respectively).

articleTitle: New materials for optical fibres based on oxochloride lead-tellurite glasses
abstract: Glasses in the $\mathrm{PbCl}_{2}-\mathrm{TeO}_{2}$ system were synthesized from high-purity starting materials. The glasses have record low absorption of hydroxyl groups, wide range of transparency and good crystallization stability. The materials are promising for drawing optical fibers.

articleTitle: Optical properties of self assembled aligned single walled carbon nanotubes
abstract: The self – assembly method was used to prepare aligned single - walled carbon nanotubes for application as a saturable absorber in ultrashort pulses lasers. The alignment of nanotubes was investigated by polarized Raman spectroscopy. Moreover, the nonlinear characteristics of the prepared aligned nanotubes film were compared to typical film with random nanotubes. The saturable absorber modulation depth has increased by 6% due to the alignment features.

articleTitle: Time-resolved fluorescence microscopy of QDs in investigations of endolysosome acidification
abstract: Endolysosomeacidification was assessed by time-resolved fluorescence microscopy (FLIM) using quantum dots targeted by epidermal growth factor (EGF-QDs). It has been shown that the interpretation of the results of changes in the QD fluorescence lifetime using the proton pump inhibitor BafA1 depends on the method of its administration. Also, some additional factors in endolysosomes can affect lifetime of QDs besides pH.

articleTitle: Advanced thin films of gallium selenide
abstract: GaSe films were synthesized by PECVD. The morphology, structural, luminescent and electrophysical properties of the resulting material were studied for its further use in a wide range of optical and optoelectronic applications and in advanced semiconductor devices. Raman spectra prove formation of the gallium monoselenide.

articleTitle: Experimental study of ultrafast laser-induced phenomena in gold
abstract: Intense ultrashort laser pulses can drive the electrons and the lattice in a solid material far out of equilibrium creating a highly excited matter with extraordinary properties. Here, we report on an experimental approach to study the relaxation of electrons in a bulk gold using time-resolved pump-probe reflectivity measurements with phase-sensitive signal detection in a wide range of absorbed energy densities ranging more than two orders of magnitude. As a result, the process of electron relaxation in gold can be seamlessly studied with femtosecond time resolution in a wide range of initial electron temperatures ranging from several tens to several thousands of kelvins by implying appropriate models of transient thermal, mechanical and optical properties. As far as we know, the experimental validation of the theories existing at present time on behavior of such crucial values as electron-phonon coupling parameter, electron thermal conductivity and electron heat capacity is almost lacking in gold driven far out of equilibrium with elevated electrons temperatures ranging from 1 to 20 kK.

articleTitle: Influence of cascaded processes on frequency doubling process
abstract: We show that weak third harmonic generation, caused by cascaded processes, may influence the frequency doubling both in negative and positive ways. Observing of these two cases are discussed.

articleTitle: Iodine Optical Frequency Standard with Hybrid Frequency Stabilization System on a High-Finesse Cavity
abstract: Wedemonstrate a method to combine a molecular iodine absolute frequency reference with a high-finesse optical cavity to take advantage of the frequency stability properties of both systems at different timescales. The result is a frequency-stabilized single Nd:YAG laser with the long-term and short-term stability levels of the iodine frequency reference and optical cavity, respectively. Experimental results show cavity-limited instability $5 \cdot 10^{-15}$ at time scales of 1 s and iodine instability below $10^{-15}$ for observation times of $10^{4} \mathrm{~s}$.

articleTitle: Laser formation of photocatalytically active TiO2 coating
abstract: The development of simple and inexpensive methods for creating catalytically active platforms is an important task for their practical application in the decomposition of organic pollutants, hydrogen production, etc. In this study, we use a ns laser ablation technique to obtain TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layer with a controlled ratio of anatase and rutile on the surface of titanium plate. We evaluate their photocatalytic efficiency in degradation of methylene blue dye under UV irradiation. The results of our experiments show that increasing the effective exposure time leads to an enlargement of the relief with simultaneous reducing the anatase phase content on the surface. Conversely, samples with higher anatase phase content exhibit superior catalytic activity due to the synergistic effect. The simplicity and high control of proposed technology suggests its potential for practical applications.

articleTitle: Mechanisms of the photodynamic effect with polycationic photosensitizers on the foci of bacterial and oncological diseases
abstract: This work presents the results of studies of the features, mechanisms and effectiveness of the photodynamic effect of PS based on polycationic derivatives of long-wave phthalocyanines and synthetic bacteriochlorin on bacteria, bacterial biofilms, tumor cells and experimental animal tumor model.

articleTitle: Tissue Exposure to Laser Pulses Delivered by Sapphire Medical Instruments: Advantages for Laser Coagulation and Ablation
abstract: In this work, we discuss the advantages of sapphire shaped crystals for manufacturing of medical instruments, in particular, capillary needles for interstitial laser therapy. The application of them for tissue ablation and coagulation is discussed.

articleTitle: Divalent copper as the possible active center for solid-state NIR lasers
abstract: We were able to observe an intense, broadband photoluminescence in different crystal hosts, doped with $\mathrm {C u}^{2+}$. These matrices include corundum (alpha-Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>), different spinels: $\mathrm {M g A l}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{4}, \mathrm{MgGa}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{4}, \mathrm{ZnAl}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{4}, \mathrm{ZnGa}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{4}$, spinel-like compounds $\mathrm{LiAl}_{5} \mathrm{O}_{8}, \mathrm{LiGa}_{5} \mathrm{O}_{8}$, perovskites $\mathrm{LaAlO}_{3}, \mathrm{GdAlO}_{3}$. The main common feature of these materials is the large magnitude of the crystal field, which contributes to the appearance of photoluminescence. Otherwise, the strong electron-phonon coupling in the ground state due to the manifestation of the Jahn-Teller effect can lead to photoluminescence quenching due to the high rate of non-radiative relaxation. It has also been demonstrated that codoping with divalent ions dramatically enhances the photoluminescence of copper in corundum and perovskites.

articleTitle: Lasers with cavities coupled by a Bragg grating
abstract: A comprehensive view of the problem of optical interaction of radiation developing in systems with several cavities is presented. Static and dynamic gratings in the lasers based on narrowband and broadband active media are considered. A number of practically implemented systems are shown and fundamental limitations are indicated.

articleTitle: Experimental research of an on-board laser acceleration measurements for the gravitational field parameters estimation on cubesate nanosatelite
abstract: The paper considers the possibility of constructing a device for a acceleration measurement based on an optical interferometer instead of a capacitive measuring system. The design of polarization single-frequency interferometer is considered. The layout of the accelerometer sensing element and a bench for measuring its sensitivity are also described. The results of the study are presented and prove the possibility of achieving sensitivity not worse than $10^{-8} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$.

articleTitle: On investigation femtosecond laser writing of defects in hexagonal boron nitride
abstract: BN have attracted a lot of attention due to their unique properties: optical detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) and single-photon emission (SPE) at room temperature. In this work, we present the results of our ongoing investigation on h -BN defects, including femtosecond laser writing for defect creation.

articleTitle: Controlled Photosensitizer-free Singlet Oxygen Release for Biomedical Applications
abstract: Numerous studies have been published that discuss the triggering of apoptosis and the enhancement of mitochondrial respiration through laser illumination and singlet oxygen production in different cells and tissues. However, a significant gap in understanding remains, and it is crucial to pinpoint the precise mechanisms of laser irradiation effects. In this paper, we share our findings in exploring this area.

articleTitle: Study of the capabilities of high-power UV and Blue LEDs for Pumping Coumarin Dyes laser
abstract: High-power AlGaInN LEDs are of interest for pumping of dyes lasers. In this regard, comprehensive studies of the power and spectral characteristics of LEDs in short-pulse modes used to laser pump were carried out. The energy capabilities and spectral properties of LED excitation of coumarin dyes were revealed.

articleTitle: Growth, Structure, Thermal Properties and Spectroscopy of Tm3+-doped MgMoO4 Laser Crystal
abstract: $\mathrm{Tm}^{3+}$-doped MgMoO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> crystal was grown by Czochralski. Thermal properties of crystal were determined. Spectroscopic studies were shown broad emission band in 1.6 $2.15 \mu \mathrm{m}$ region (the ${ }^{3} \mathrm{~F}_{4} \rightarrow{ }^{3} \mathrm{H}_{6}$ transition) and a long ${ }^{3} \mathrm{~F}_{4}$ excited-state lifetime that makes this crystal promising for lasers.

articleTitle: Theoretical research of a potassium diode-pumped alkali laser
abstract: The results of computational and theoretical studies of diode-pumped alkali laser parameters are presented. A mathematical model of the pumped alkali laser is constructed, a numerical solution of the equations of kinetics and laser radiation transfer considering the width of the pumping spectrum is given, and the optimal parameters of the laser installation were obtained, at which the calculated “light-to-light” efficiency is more than $50 \%$.

articleTitle: Laser noise reduction with additional filtering resonator
abstract: We study quantum computing technology based on neutral rubidium atoms. Effect of Rydberg blockade is use in order to achieve entanglement of two qubits. Rydberg states are obtained by shining on the array of cold atoms with two lasers. Stability of the driving lasers and noise reduction are required for high fidelity of quantum gates. Theoretical analysis and experimental setup of PDH-locking scheme with additional filtering resonator will be presented.

articleTitle: Imaging photoplethysmography to study blood supply in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus and systemic scleroderma
abstract: The parameters of facial blood supply were studied in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus and systemic scleroderma using a non-contact imaging photoplethysmography method synchronized with an electrocardiogram. Statistically significant differences in the amplitude and time of arrival of the pulse wave to different areas of the face were revealed in sick patients compared with the control group.

articleTitle: Optimization of single-frequency continuous wave self-sweeping fiber laser based on separated gain and absorption dynamics gratings
abstract: We report on the optimization of a self-sweeping single-frequency fiber laser with continuous-wave (CW) intensity dynamics, lasing in the L-band telecommunications region with a wavelength of 1607 nm and a sweep range of 2.45 nm. The laser output power was increased to 4 mW and frequency step was reduced to 10.3 MHz. The single-frequency self-sweeping fiber source developed in this work can be used for optical frequency domain reflectometry.

articleTitle: Coexistence of discrete-variable phase-time coding QKD with intense classical signals over 60 km
abstract: This paper presents the results of an experimental study of the perfomance of the QKD system in coexistence with strong C-band signals in a single fiber. The possibility of QKD over a distance up to 60 km with a total power of classical channels up to 20 mW has been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Laser synthesis of cobalt-based nanoparticles in gaseous media and magnetic field
abstract: This paper presents the results of laser ablation of cobalt targets in a magnetic field in argon and air. The experimental setup, processing parameters are described and the results of scanning electron microscopy are presented, which allow us to estimate the size and shape of particles.

articleTitle: Laser speckle contrast imaging for intraoperative blood flow monitoring during neurovascular surgery
abstract: Assessment of blood flow in neurovascular interventions is crucial for minimizing postoperative complications. This paper presents a comparison of laser speckle contrast imaging and indocyanine green angiography in the context of neurovascular interventions.

articleTitle: Automatic laser beam pointing and positioning system with 4 wide-aperture folding mirrors on motorized gimbal mounts
abstract: The semi-automatic system for laser beam alignment was developed and researched. The alignment system was used to make the laser beam follow the predetermined path through the optical scheme. The system allowed to control the pointing and positioning of the beam as well as tip-tilt and overall curvature of the wavefront.

articleTitle: The zones of stable generation of dissipative solitons in fiber lasers depending on the cavity dispersion and the modulation depth of the saturable absorber
abstract: The zones of stable pulsed generation of dissipative solitons in fiber lasers are determined depending on the group delay dispersion of the resonator and the modulation depth of the saturable absorber. It is concluded that the possibility of stable pulse generation depends on the dynamics of the modulation depth changes of the saturable absorber in fiber laser during multiple passes of the pulse through the laser resonator. Taking into account the dependence of the modulation depth of a saturable absorber on the pulse duration that allowed us to find the zones of unstable solutions where pulse generation is absent due to a significant dispersion broadening of the pulse in the laser cavity.

articleTitle: Laser functionalization of carbon nanotubes with LaB6 particles
abstract: This work experimentally investigates the effect of functionalization of carbon nanotubes array with LaB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> nanoparticles on the electrophysical properties. A hybrid nanomaterial was based on a vertical nanotubes array functionalized with LaB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> nanoparticles. Nanotubes were structured by pulsed laser irradiation (energy density 0.15 J/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). The functionalized hybrid nanomaterial had a maximum field emission current of 55 μA.

articleTitle: Laser acceleration of charged particles from preplasma.
abstract: In this work, we study plasma that arises during the interaction of laser radiation with a target. Depending on the parameters of the laser pulse, the resulting plasma can have a significant impact on the efficiency of acceleration of charged particles.

articleTitle: Study of a New 2-μm Laser Crystal Tm, Li:ZnWO4
abstract: ${T m}^{3+}, \mathbf{L i}^{+}: \mathbf{Z n W O}_{4}$ single-crystal was grown by the Czochralski (Cz) method. The actual concentrations of the dopants were measured. Dispersions and temperature coefficients of the refractive indices (RI), as well as the mechanical strength characteristics of the crystal were measured. Spectroscopic studies of the crystal were carried out. The first laser operation above 2 $\mu \mathrm{m}$ at this crystal was obtained.

articleTitle: Topology of light polarization-ellipse strips in near-field and nonlinear optics
abstract: We applied topology methods to study in details the properties of the strips, formed by polarization ellipses which are built on closed contours in non-paraxial monochromatic light field. The twisting number of the strip is shown to be dependent on the topology and orientation of its construction contour, the linking coefficient between the contour and polarization singularity lines and the properties of the non-paraxial electromagnetic field itself. Analytical expressions for the twisting number is found for the simplest cases of the strips.

articleTitle: Methods of parallel mode decomposition for investigating real-time mode dynamics
abstract: In this work we numerically compared digital hologram generation methods for the purpose of fiber mode decomposition. After that, the most accurate method was implemented in the experimental analysis of real-time intermodal dynamics in a Raman fiber laser.

articleTitle: A Source of Ultracold 87Rb Atoms For an Atom Interferometer-Gravimeter
abstract: In this work, we created a source of ultracold atoms for a quantum interferometer-gravimeter. A cloud of $10^{7}-10^{8}$ atoms with the temperature of around 6 uK was obtained. An effective selection of rubidium atoms in the nonmagnetic sub-state was carried out.

articleTitle: Laser initiated generation of x-rays and neutrons from microdroplet plasma
abstract: abstract-The concept of maximizing synchrotron X rays and DD neutron yield from laser-heated large volume of microdroplet target by matching the focal spot size and structural scales of target to the laser pulse intensity was confirmed.

Author Keywords: laser driven neutron and X ray sources

articleTitle: Spatio-temporal properties of an atomic medium interaction with vortex vector fields of femtosecond duration
abstract: The interaction of a thin neon gas medium localized in the focal region of sharply focused laser fields with various amplitude and structural parameters was studied. The fields in the focal plane were described using the Richards-Wolf vector focusing theory. The generated harmonics were studied in terms of intensity and polarization state as a function of distance between the focal plane and the detector and in the lateral and sagittal planes. Optimal conditions for the generation of structured high harmonics were determined.

articleTitle: UV nitrogen laser pumped by a joint pulsed longitudinal electric and inductive discharge
abstract: The joint method of a nitrogen laser pumping by electric longitudinal and inductive discharges has been proposed and experimentally implemented. The inductive discharge was formed at the stage of charging the sharpening capacitors and played the role of the API of the active volume. UV laser radiation corresponding to the transitions of 0-0($\lambda$=337.1 nm) and 0-1($\lambda$=357.7 nm) 2+ systems of bands of nitrogen molecules was obtained. The energy of laser radiation reached 2 mJ at a nitrogen pressure of 9…10 Torr. Enhancing pumping by an inductive discharge made it possible to significantly increase the operating efficiency of an electric-discharge nitrogen laser, and in addition, improve the quality of the laser beam.

articleTitle: Wide-band diffuse reflectance spectroscopy with a self-calibrating fiber-optic probe
abstract: We report on creation of a diffuse optical spectroscopy (DOS) setup in a wide VIS-NIR spectral range with a contact fiber-optic probe using a self-calibration technique. A four measurement procedure employing two source and two collection fibers arranged symmetrically allows to calculate extinction spectrum of investigated tissue, excluding DOS instrumental characteristics and reducing the influence of absorption inhomogeneities on a tissue surface. High accuracy of a measured extinction spectra allows one to account for more tissue chromophores and precisely assess tissue physiological properties. The proposed system was applied successfully in preliminary in vivo studies.

articleTitle: Hybridly polarized optical vortices
abstract: In this work numerically using Richards-Wolf equation and experimentally using spatial light modulator we have investigated optical vortices with hybrid polarization. The polarization of these beams combines azimuthal polarization and circular polarization.

articleTitle: Two-stage deep laser cooling of Yb-171 ion in a radio frequency trap without using a magnetic field
abstract: The new two-stage scheme for deep laser cooling of ${}^{171} \mathbf{Y b}^{+}$ is suggested. This scheme apart from well-known approaches does not require application of magnetic field. The suggested approach opens up possibility for precise control of magnetic field for further progress in optical frequency standards and quantum computing.

articleTitle: SOA-based reservoir computing
abstract: We present a novel reservoir computing approach in which single nonlinear device - semiconductor optical amplifier, replaces the entire nonlinear reservoir to perform computations, without the conventional use of a delay loop. To study the performance of the proposed scheme, we use it for the benchmark prediction task of learning the Mackey-Glass chaotic attractor.

articleTitle: Characterization of solid hydrogen isotopes layer parameters in cryogenic target for inertial confinement fusion
abstract: This paper presents the results of development of the optic shadow and X-ray phase-contrast characterization methods of the parameters of the fuel layer in a cryogenic target for inertial confinement fusion.

articleTitle: Mechanism of Rabi-excitation of discrete modes outside the spectral line of a superradiant laser
abstract: By means of numerical modeling of nonlinear and analytical solution of linearized Maxwell-Bloch equations, we find an intriguing regime of a superradiant laser with a symmetric low-Q Fabry-Perot cavity equipped with a distributed feedback of counter-propagating waves. We find that, in a wide range of parameters, there is lasing of a strongly-asymmetric self-modulated powerful polariton mode accompanied by excitation of several almost symmetric weak polariton or electromagnetic modes. The frequency of the powerful mode is approximately coincides with a center of the laser spectral line, and the frequencies of the weak modes are outside the spectral line of an active medium. We show that such a lasing takes place due to formation of a self-consistent inhomogeneous asymmetric grating of population inversion of active centers that provides undamped Rabi oscillations of the population inversion and dipole moments of centers. The grating makes the powerful ‘central’ mode strongly asymmetric, and the Rabi oscillations of active centers excite the weak ‘sideband’ modes due to the quadratic resonant nonlinearity of the two-level active medium.

articleTitle: Vortex-Generating Light-Induced Phase Converter in Azobenzene Polymer
abstract: The formation of the modified area, which acts as phase converter for vortex generation, in the amorphous thin layer of the azo-containing polymer under the action of structured light beam is considered. The optical axes are produced in accordance with the polarization structure of the pump light beam. The beam with radial polarization induces the axially-symmetric optical axis distribution (similar to q-plate) with negative optical anisotropy proportional to the light beam intensity. We demonstrate that this light-induced modification can efficiently convert the probe Gaussian beam into optical vortex with the topological charge 2.

articleTitle: New mechanisms in stem cells differentiation and tissue regeneration discovered by optical imaging
abstract: Using FLIM and multiphoton fluorescence microscopy we investigated the metabolic status in mesenchymal stem cells during adipogenic, osteogenic and chondrogenic differentiation, the metabolic activity and intracellular pH in iPSC differentiating in dermal, epidermal, neuronal directions, in 3D neurospheres from iPSCs, in neural spheroids with Down syndrome, metabolic changes in living islets of Langerhans, and during liver regeneration.

articleTitle: Laser synthesis of iron-based nanoparticles in gaseous media and magnetic field by nanosecond pulses
abstract: The paper presents the results of the ablative synthesis of iron nanoparticles in an argon medium under the action of nanosecond laser pulses. Nanoparticles were collected and deposited using a magnetic field.

articleTitle: Method for Measuring Pairwise Affinity of Substantially Non-complementary Oligonucleotides
abstract: Strand commutation based on low-affinity interactions of non-complementary nucleic acids is a unique tool for data processing through DNA. Here we demonstrate a method for measuring pairwise oligonucleotide affinity, which allows us to create accurate predictive resources. We used a range of optical techniques, including UV- and fluorescence spectroscopy, to determine the binding constant in DNA duplex of non-complementary strands.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of supercontinuum generation in all-fiber Er-doped master oscillator fiber amplifier
abstract: Numerical study based on nonlinear Schrodinger equation was conducted to optimize the characteristics of all-fiber master oscillator fiber amplifier based on erbium-doped fiber laser. The generation of supercontinuum in high-nonlinearity fiber (HNLF) was achieved. The optimization of HNLF length, and the average power of amplified pulses led to 1155 nm spectral width at -20dB.

articleTitle: IR spectroscopy for hematology
abstract: Currently, there is an increase in the number of oncohematological diseases. Simple and reliable screening methods are required for their effective diagnosis. One of the promising and rapidly developing approaches is IR spectroscopy of various samples of biomaterials. In this work, we analyzed the IR spectra of blood serum from patients with multiple myeloma, chronic lymphocytic leukemia and healthy donors.

articleTitle: Hybrid amplification of highly-chirped pulses around 1.3 micron in an all-fiber configuration
abstract: We report the amplification of highly-chirped dissipative solitons around $1.3 \mu \mathrm{m}$ in an all fiber configuration by two methods: Stimulated Raman Scattering in a standard passive fiber and using active centers in a Bi-doped fiber pumped by CW radiation. The former provides spectrally uniform amplification resulting in good quality of compressed pulse, and the latter provides a 16 -fold net gain.

articleTitle: Influence of anti-reflection and partial-high-reflection coatings on characteristics of quantum cascade lasers in 4-5μm range
abstract: We analyze the influence of optical coatings on the electro-optical characteristics of quantum cascade lasers. We compare light-current characteristics of devices without and with different combinations of optical coatings. The highest output power is achieved with combination of anti- and high-reflection coatings, while the lowest threshold with partial-high- and highreflection coatings.

articleTitle: Ternary N-based nanostructures: growth and properties
abstract: Nanostructures based on III-N materials are promising candidates for ultraviolet and visible light emitting devices. In particular, ternary InGaN nanowires (NWs) grown on semiconductor wafers perfectly fit to optoelectronic applications. In this paper, we will show that InGaN/Si NWs system is quite sensitive to the growth conditions and even a small change in the growth temperature leads to a significant change in morphological properties of the NWs and also shifts the photoluminescence spectra from blue to red regions with In content in the NWs increase. We will also demonstrate that, under specific growth temperatures, InGaN NWs may be grown in a form of core-shell structure where indium composition in the core is much higher than In content in the core one.

articleTitle: Devising the Ways to Expand Throughput of a Directly Modulated Long-Wavelength VCSEL
abstract: The comparison of the two approaches to increasing vertical cavity surface emitting laser throughput, including the standard pulse amplitude modulation and a new technology associated with the use of optical injection locking, which provides a significant expansion of the slave laser’s direct modulation bandwidth, is proposed and validated by the simulation and measurements.

articleTitle: Frequency analysis of the auto tuning system for multistage laser complexes
abstract: A well-known problem of multi-stage laser systems is deviations of radiation from a given direction during its transmission between sections. To automatically correct the radiation direction, an auto-tuning system has been developed based on piezoelectric actuators with feedback through a four-section photodiode. It is demonstrated that the developed system operates reliably at low disturbance frequencies. At the same time, there is an upper frequency, above which the system does not process disturbances.

articleTitle: Size-dependent properties of InAs quantum dots in Si
abstract: The self-assembled InAs quantum dots (QDs) in silicon were fabricated by solid source molecular beam epitaxy on $\mathrm{Si}(\mathbf{1 0 0}) 4^{\circ}$ substrates using Wolmer-Veber growth mode. The PL spectra exhibit $1.6 \mu \mathrm{m}$ emission from InAs quantum dots at 10 K. The size-depended luminescence behavior of QDs was observed. As the InAs coverage decreased from 2 to 0.5 monolayers (ML), the photoluminescence peak shifted from 1620 to 1580 nm and increased monotonously.

articleTitle: Photoluminescence enhancement of InGaN core-shell nanowires via wet chemical treatment
abstract: It has been revealed that removing the shell of spontaneously formed InGaN nanowires increases the amplitude and narrows their emission spectrum. It has been established that radiative recombination dominates in the nanowires. And the dependence of the integrated photoluminescence intensity on the pump power for nanowires after etching is superlinear in comparison with the initial ones.

articleTitle: Pleochroism of β-BBO Crystals Grown from NaBaBO3, Vanadium, and Molybdenum-Based Melt Solutions: Visible and Infrared Spectral Range
abstract: We present study on optical properties of $\boldsymbol{\beta}$-BBO crystals grown from three distinct melt solutions: initial NaBaBO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, $\mathrm{NaBaBO}_{3}-\mathrm{V}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{5}$, and $\mathrm{BaMoO}_{4}-\mathrm{BaF}_{2}$. Polarized VIS and FTIR spectra as well as with Raman scattering spectra were used. The mean absorption coefficient for e-waves within the $1.5-2.0 \mu \mathrm{m}$ range measured $0.015,0.03$, and $0.008 \mathrm{~cm}^{-1}$ for initial, vanadium, and molybdenum based grown crystals.

articleTitle: Measurement of absolute frequencies of transitions in thulium atoms
abstract: Clock transition at $1.14 \mu \mathrm{m}$ in neutral thulium is a promising candidate for compact and robust transportable optical clock due to its extremely low sensitivity to external electric and magnetic fields. Cold Tm atoms are now used in optical lattice clocks, quantum simulators and for the study of Bose-Einstein condensation and cold collision physics. In this work, we discuss experimentally measured absolute frequencies of the two transitions at 410.6 nm and 530.7 nm, used for laser cooling of thulium atoms, transition at 418.8 nm used for optical pumping and clock transition at 1140 nm. Using accurate laser spectroscopy in an ensemble of cold thulium atoms, we measured frequencies of these transitions using an optical frequency comb, which was referenced to an active hydrogen maser. Transition frequencies were measured with an uncertainty at one tenth of their natural linewidth, which is sufficient for cooling and pumping of thulium atoms. The uncertainty of the clock transition frequency is 30 Hz, which was limited by the maser frequency calibration with GNSS. Our results can find application in existing experiments with cold thulium atoms and especially in new projects.

articleTitle: The Nonlinear Optical Properties of the Water Clusters with Oxygen Molecule
abstract: Amazing growing the elements of polarizability tenzor and the first hyperpolarizability tenzor of the water clusters after oxygen molecule capture was predicted by ab initio quantum – chemical calculations. This phenomenon may be the reason of the new spectral component near 3000 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> appearance on the water-air interface found by picosecond stimulated Raman scattering at 532 nm excitation.

Author Keywords: cubic tensor of the first hyperpolarizability

articleTitle: OCT monitoring of scattering kinetics in tissue phantoms at optical clearing with depth resolution
abstract: Using gelatin phantoms, a method for measuring the scattering coefficient of homogeneous samples with depth resolution under optical clearing was developed and tested. The method is based on the restoration of depth profiles of an optical coherence tomography (OCT) signal, taking into account the axial point spread function, as well as the correction of incomplete attenuation of the probing radiation in the deep part of the OCT sensing window. Using this method, an increase in the characteristic time of water diffusion in the phantom during the formation of intermolecular cross-links of collagen is shown.

articleTitle: Density functional theory study of In wetting layer formation during droplet epitaxy growth of InAs/AlGaAs quantum dots
abstract: In this work we study In wetting layer formation during droplet epitaxy of InAs QDs with goal of explaining anomalous behavior where increase in content of chemically active Al in AlGaAs substrate leads to increase in surface mobility of In adatoms that affects final distribution of QDs. DFT simulations showed that lack of As during wetting layer formation characteristic for droplet epitaxy allows In adatoms to form dimer rows that, as we hypothesize, makes their electron density more likely to shift towards Al atoms in substrate and away from surface decreasing strength of bonding of future adatoms and thus increasing their surface mobility.

articleTitle: Fiber femtosecond frequency comb for measuring the dispersion of optical elements
abstract: The results of the measuring the dispersion parameter D for the SMF-28 fiber using a three-wave single-arm interferometer (SAI) and a femtosecond fiber frequency comb (FFFC) stabilized to a $\mathbf{Y b}^{+}$single-ion optical frequency standard are presented in this work. The second-order group velocity dispersion (GVD) was taken into account for the first time. This approach can be applied to any optical fibers and bulk optical elements, such as crystals, glasses, chirped mirrors, etc.

articleTitle: Annealing temperature effect on the GaAs nanowire growth on the FIB-modified Si substrate
abstract: Inthis work, it was found that in addition to the strong dose dependence of the nanowire parameters grown within the ion beam treatment area, the annealing temperature also has a significant effect. It is shown that an increase of the annealing temperature from 600 to $750^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ leads, on the one hand, to an increase of the nanowire density up to $\sim 40 \mu \mathrm{m}^{-2}$ at the maximum dose value. On the other hand, this leads to an increase in the proportion of vertically oriented nanowires up to 100%.

articleTitle: Mathematical simulation of uniform heating of biological tissues by laser radiation
abstract: The description of thermal damage to biological tissues is based on the Arrhenius formalism. Experimental measurements of Arrhenius parameters $(\ln A$ and $T_{c r}$) are conducted under the assumption of homogeneously degraded samples. In this work, the degradation processes of biological tissue under conditions of heating with air, water and optical radiation were simulated. Optical heating has demonstrated high precision in retrieving the degradation kinetics parameters at different sample thicknesses and degradation times compared to convective methods (air and water). The simulation highlights the advantage of uniform optical heating to study the kinetics of thermal degradation in biological tissues.

articleTitle: Measurement of Dispersion Characteristics and Q-factors of Optical Microresonators
abstract: We perform an experimental measurement of dispersion characteristics and quality factors of optical integrated silicon nitride ring microresonators with different geometries.

articleTitle: High-energy single-crystal Fe:CdTe laser operating in the wavelength range of 5.3-6.0 μm
abstract: The generation characteristics of a laser with a Fe:CdTe single crystal grown by a modified vertical gradient freeze method and subjected to high-temperature treatment as an active element have been studied. The possibility of efficient pumping using Fe:ZnSe or deuterium fluoride laser has been demonstrated. The broadband generation in the range of 5.3-6.0 $\mu \mathrm{m}$ with a maximum energy of up to 0.35 J per pulse has been obtained.

articleTitle: Image Transmission With Parallel Array of Artificial Spiking Neurons Based on VCSEL and SPAD
abstract: An optoelectronic artificial spiking neuron (ASN) based on a vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL) and single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) operating in the regime of a probabilistic response in combination with a software-implemented neural network of parallel-connected ASNs allows one to transmit images through a neural network virtually with no distortion. The method is based on the coding of image intensity gradations into the pulse triggering probability from a SPAD with a subsequent summation of output pulses from SPAD.

articleTitle: Analytical approximation for light bullets in multi-core fibers
abstract: We propose a theoretical approach to study the multicore fiber propagation dynamics of optical pulses near a stationary solution known as “light bullet”. A system of coupled non-conservative nonlinear Schrödinger equations is used as a mathematical model. An approximate analytical stationary solution for this system of equations is found and studied.

articleTitle: Antireflection microstructures on ZnSe fabricated by wet-etching-assisted femtosecond laser ablation
abstract: We report an increase in ZnSe transmittance up to 98% in mid- and far-IR using antireflection microstructures (ARMs) fabricated with femtosecond laser ablation assisted with wet chemical etching.

articleTitle: Quantum-cascade laser emitting at 8μm: epi-growth and characterization
abstract: The results on fabrication and optical characterization of lattice-matched to InP quantum-cascade laser emitting at $8 \mu \mathrm{m}$ are reported. The high current dynamic range is observed for lasers with four cleaved facets.

articleTitle: Increasing BOTDA precision using correlation image processing methods
abstract: In this work, we demonstrate improving the precision of correlation methods for Brillouin frequency shift (BFS) extraction in distributed fiber optic sensors by applying the algorithms in 2D space. The use of several spectra at once to calculate correlation functions made it possible to increase the precision of the BOTDA. The developed approaches have proven themselves to be the best when processing spectra with low frequency resolution (obtained with high frequency scan step FS).

articleTitle: Molecular detection using plasmonic nanostructures of particular geometry
abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) is used to detect substances in low concentration. Neglecting the chemical enhancement phenomena, the model of polystyrene structures with silver nanoparticles was used to obtain Raman signals from molecules of rhodamine 6G (R6G). In the current work different geometries of these plasmonic structures were investigated and their ability to enhance the electromagnetic field was compared.

articleTitle: Erbium laser for modifacation dentin surface of the tooth
abstract: Indications for usage of Erbium family lasers in dentistry are increasing. The success of root canal treatment depends on removing bacterias and smear layer for better adhesion of sealer. Usage lasers in endodontical treatment enhancing success for the treatment in long-term follow up.

articleTitle: Optical Crystals and Ceramics Based on the AgCl0.25Br0.75 - TlI System as Scintillator Materials
abstract: The work is devoted to the study of the phase diagram of the $\mathbf{A g C l}_{0.25} \mathbf{B r}_{0.75}$ - TII system. Based on the results, homogeneous and heterogeneous regions were established where it is possible to grow single crystals and synthesize optical ceramics. Single crystals and ceramics of this system are intended for use as fibers and scintillators.

articleTitle: 1550 nm Few-Mode Laser Diodes
abstract: The main characteristics of 1550 nm few-mode laser diodes with aperture width $20 \mu \mathrm{m}$ and different cavity lengths (power, electrical, spectral and spatial characteristics) were measured. It is shown that there are two ranges of pump currents in which the characteristics of lasers behave differently: the first current range corresponds to operation in a low-mode mode, in which a scatter in the output characteristics of lasers is observed; in the second range the laser operates predictably and stably.

articleTitle: Optical measurements in vitro and in vivo of erythrocyte aggregation parameters in patients with different pathologies
abstract: Erythrocyte aggregation plays a vital role in blood flow. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of laser-optical techniques in measuring erythrocyte aggregation parameters in healthy donors and patients suffering from different diseases.

articleTitle: Gratings induced by few-cycle light pulses
abstract: This talk revisits our recent results on population density grating formation and control in a resonant medium by extremely short light pulses down to single and subcycle durations.

articleTitle: Ultrashort pulse laser based Raman DTS for midrange FUT high spatial resolution measurements
abstract: We report on a study of distributed fiber-optic temperature sensor based on Raman scattering, in which an ultrashort-pulse fiber laser is used as a source of optical probing pulses. Together with the short pulse duration and pulse repetition rate decimation scheme using an acousto-optical modulator, we were able to achieve experimentally 0.3 m spatial resolution over more than 8 km long fiber-under-test.

articleTitle: THz polarization-sensitive solid immersion microscopy
abstract: In our work we demonstrate a reflection-mode polarization-sensitive terahertz (THz) microscope based on solid immersion effect. We apply it to study THz anisotropy of test media with $0.15 \lambda$ spatial resolution, including freshly excised rat brain, where the most pronounced birefringence is observed in the Corpus callosum. The obtained results show the prospects of applying THz polarization-sensitive microscopy in medical imaging.

articleTitle: Optical-Magnetic Characterization of IgG and Nanoparticles for Rapid Biosensor Development: Detection of Cardiac Markers and Mycotoxins
abstract: This study introduces a novel method for characterizing immunoglobulins G (IgG) and functionalized nanoparticles crucial in biosensor development. Utilizing label-free low-coherence interferometry and magnetic lateral flow immunoassay, the method enables kinetic studies, IgG sorption density quantification, and functional nanoparticle characterization. Demonstrated efficacy in creating highly sensitive assay systems for mycotoxins and cardiovascular biomarkers highlights the method’s potential impact across diverse compounds. With promising results in sensitivity, dynamic range, and analysis time, this approach offers versatility for advancing rapid biosensor systems.

articleTitle: Luminescence properties of Er3+:Y2O3 laser ceramics
abstract: 5-15 at. $\% \mathrm{Er}^{3+}: \mathrm{Y}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}$ sesquioxide ceramics were fabricated and studied. Transmission spectra of the samples were obtained in a wide spectral range. Ceramics exhibit high transmittance values (up to $80 \%$). Luminescence spectra were obtained at 1.5 and $3 \mu \mathrm{m}$. the intensity of the luminescence line at a wavelength of about 1.5 $\mu \mathrm{m}$ increases with decreasing concentration.

articleTitle: High-power QCL for 8 μm spectral range
abstract: We study quantum-cascade lasers with active region designs based on strained and lattice-matched heterostructures. Lasers based on strained well/barrier pairs demonstrate improved efficiency, temperature stability and record-high optical power.

articleTitle: Structural Laser Diagnostics for Ordered Substances, Optical Materials, and Nanosystems
abstract: New prospects for laser polarization-optical diagnostics of structural features and fluctuations of ordered substances, selective reflected light, optical functional materials and elements are considered.

articleTitle: Fast-Slow Light Effects of Chirped Laser Pulses in Epsilon-Near-Zero Nanorods Based Metamaterials
abstract: Experimental and numerical studies of fast and slow light effects under the propagation of chirped femtosecond laser pulses in epsilon-near-zero metamaterials based on the array of metal nanorods are carried out. We show that the chirp brings about additional control over the fast and slow light regimes.

articleTitle: Effect of Topology on the Optical Properties of Quantum Confined Semiconductor Nanocrystals
